“I assure you that no one will be allowed to intimidate or harass you from participating in the election. Any thug or hoodlum caught disrupting the process will face the full weight of the law.

“Do not be distracted by rumours that the election will be violent. The current administration’s tenure is coming to an end, and by August 15, a new era of development will begin,” he said.

The campaign train later moved to Ikirun, where Oyebamiji addressed supporters at the town hall before proceeding to Iree, Ada, Aagba and Iragbiji as part of his statewide campaign tour.

World.title: Gunmen kill teenager, rustle cattle in fresh Benue attack
World.content:
Stock image

..Residents flee for safety

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

Suspected armed men have attacked Olahimu village in Ogoli Ugboju, Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue State, killing a 15-year-old boy and rustling several cattle in a fresh attack on the community.

The attack, which reportedly occurred at about 7 a.m. on Tuesday, also left one person missing, while three others who were initially unaccounted for were later found after escaping from the assailants.

The victims were said to be members of the family of the late Benue State Chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Ardo Risku Muhammad, who was killed a few weeks ago in Okudu community, Otukpo LGA, while returning from a peace meeting in neighbouring Ohimini Local Government Area.

In a statement signed by Muhammed Idris on behalf of the family, the deceased was identified as Muhammad Isiyaku, while the missing person was identified as Saidu Musa, a family labourer.

The statement added that although about 500 cattle were initially rustled, many had been recovered during search operations around the Okudu axis, while some animals were found dead and others remained missing.

According to the family, three persons initially declared missing — Muhammed Ismaiel, 17; Muhammed Hamza, 13; and a labourer, Abu Ali — were later found alive after escaping from the attackers.

The family condemned the attack and appealed to the Benue State Government, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to intensify efforts to rescue the missing labourer and recover the remaining stolen cattle.

“We strongly condemn this act of violence, killing and cattle rustling. We appeal to the Benue State Government, the Nigeria Police Force, DSS and all security agencies to urgently intensify efforts to locate Saidu Musa and recover the remaining missing cattle.

“We also call for increased security presence in Olahimu, Ogoli Ugboju and other border communities to prevent further attacks and a breakdown of law and order,” the statement read.

Confirming the incident, the Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area, Maxwell Ogiri, said he received a distress call while the attack was ongoing and immediately alerted security agencies and community leaders.

According to him, “Idris called me that an attack on their herd was ongoing and that he was more concerned about the survival of his younger ones who were taking care of the cattle.

“I immediately contacted the District Head, the Divisional Police Officer and the youth leader, who mobilised to the area. Later, Idris informed me that they found one of his brothers dead, while the others who were initially missing were eventually located, except one labourer. The cows were nowhere to be found.”

Ogiri lamented the rising cases of cattle rustling and armed attacks in the area, recalling that only a few days earlier, suspected bandits rustled more than 50 cattle from a private ranch in Jericho village and had also been attacking communities to loot food items and other valuables.

He said the latest attacks had forced many residents to flee their homes and abandon their farms at the peak of the farming season.

When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Udeme Edet, said she had yet to receive detailed information on the incident.

World.title: US President Trump Writes Tinubu, Lauds His Decisive Action Against Terrorists
World.content:
* Expresses his delight in standing with Nigeria in the fight against terrorism and make the nation stronger

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

United States President Donald Trump has hailed his Nigerian counterpart, Bola Tinubu, for his decisive leadership “on behalf of the Nigerian people to tackle the issues plaguing Nigeria, especially the violence affecting Christian communities”.

In a letter dated July 6, 2026 to President Tinubu, Trump declared that: “It is a true honour to stand with you in the fight against these terrorists and to make the Federal Republic of Nigeria stronger and more prosperous.”

According to a statement issued on Wednesday by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the US-Nigeria relationship flourished in recent times, with the two sides working closely in key areas, especially in tackling security challenges afflicting parts of Nigeria.

In November last year, President Trump and President Tinubu agreed to establish a Joint Working Group co-headed by the National Security Advisers of Nigeria and the United States. Through the work of the working group, the two sides agreed on several steps, including training, intelligence sharing, and joint operations to roll back terrorist activities.

A highlight of the collaboration was the May 16 coordinated attack on ISIS hideouts in the Lake Chad area, which led to the killing of the group’s top leader, Abubakar Al-Minoki, and many of his lieutenants

Last week, the US Assistant Secretary of State for Africa, Frank Garcia, visited Abuja, where he held meetings with senior government officials and pledged to strengthen the cooperation between Abuja and Washington DC in security and other areas of collaboration.

Full text of the three-paragraph letter dated July 6, 2026 reads:

“Dear Mr President,

“Thank you for your thoughtful letter. Your kind words mean a great deal to me, and I appreciate your decisive leadership on behalf of the Nigerian people. I applaud your resolve to tackle the issues plaguing your nation, especially the violence affecting Christian communities and it is a true honor to stand with you in the fight against terrorists and to make the Federal Republic of Nigeria stronger and more prosperous.

“The United States-Nigeria relationship is crucial at a time where conflict has spread across West Africa and around the world. We both share a mutual goal of confronting terrorism in all its forms, and our historic US-Nigeria 2026 Defence Cooperation Roadmap has established a robust framework to accomplish this feat.

“I am proud to have deployed the United States Special Operations Forces—among the most elite military units anywhere in the world—to equip the brave men and women in the Armed Forces of Nigeria with the skills, tools and intelligence they need to protect your homeland and ensure the safety and security of citizens, particularly those of faith who have been under attack. I look forward to our continued discussions over the course of my Presidency.”

“Sincerely,

Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America.”

World.title: Nigeria, Germany Seek Deeper Partnership in Energy, Technology, Security
World.content:
* With Germany pledging more investment in Nigeria as trade volume rises by 10%

Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Nigeria and Germany have reaffirmed their commitment in strengthening bilateral ties, with both countries exploring expanded cooperation in renewable energy, digital innovation, manufacturing, security and human capital development.

The commitment was made on Wednesday in Abuja during a bilateral meeting between Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, and Germany’s Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs, Johann Wadephul.

Welcoming the German delegation, Odumegwu-Ojukwu described Germany as one of Nigeria’s most important strategic partners in Europe, noting that decades of cooperation between both countries had been built on mutual respect, trust and shared interests.

She said Nigeria-Germany relations had grown beyond traditional diplomacy to include trade and investment, development cooperation, renewable energy, education, vocational training, science and technology, migration, culture, peace and security.

“Germany has remained one of Nigeria’s most important strategic partners in Europe. Our bilateral relations extend beyond diplomacy to encompass trade and investment, development cooperation, renewable energy, education, vocational training, science and technology, migration, culture, peace and security,” the minister said.

She noted that the partnership had become increasingly important amid growing global challenges, including geopolitical tensions, terrorism, violent extremism, climate change, irregular migration, food insecurity and economic uncertainties.

According to her, Nigeria remains committed to deepening cooperation with Germany in ways that deliver practical benefits for citizens of both countries while contributing to regional and global stability.

She highlighted renewable energy, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, infrastructure and the green economy as areas with significant opportunities for increased collaboration.

The minister also pointed to the Nigeria-Germany Bi-National Commission as a key platform for advancing bilateral relations, recalling that the 2025 session of the commission strengthened commitments to expanding cooperation across priority sectors.

She said Nigeria had continued implementing agreements reached during the commission, including economic reforms aimed at improving the investment climate, strengthening governance and encouraging private sector participation.

Odumegwu-Ojukwu also commended Germany’s longstanding support for the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), particularly in promoting regional integration, democratic governance, peace-building, conflict prevention and humanitarian assistance.

She stressed the importance of continued international cooperation in addressing regional security threats, including terrorism, violent extremism, unconstitutional changes of government and transnational organised crime.

On economic cooperation, the foreign minister said Nigeria’s economic diplomacy remained a central pillar of its foreign policy under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration.

She urged increased German investment in Nigeria’s priority sectors, including renewable energy, manufacturing, critical minerals, transport infrastructure, agriculture, digital technology and industrial development.

She further emphasised the need for stronger collaboration in education, research, innovation and technical training, describing Germany’s vocational education system as a model that could support youth empowerment in Nigeria.

“As Africa’s largest economy and most populous nation, Nigeria remains committed to working closely with Germany in advancing peace, promoting inclusive economic growth and addressing common global challenges,” she said.

Odumegwu-Ojukwu expressed confidence that the discussions would produce practical outcomes capable of further strengthening relations between both countries.

Germany on its part, reaffirmed its commitment to deepening economic and strategic ties with Nigeria, promising increased investment in key sectors of the Nigerian economy as both countries mark over six decades of diplomatic relations.

German Foreign Minister Wadephul gave the assurance while describing the relationship between both countries as a longstanding strategic partnership that has existed for more than 65 years, recalling that Germany established its embassy in Lagos just three days after Nigeria gained independence in 1960.

He said Nigeria remained Germany’s biggest European trading partner on a bilateral basis, noting that trade between the two countries recorded a 10 per cent increase in the previous year.

The German minister, who was accompanied by senior government officials and business representatives, said the Nigeria-Germany Business Forum would continue to serve as a platform for expanding commercial ties and attracting more German investors into Nigeria.

“With my visit, many more German investors will be investing in Nigeria,” he said, highlighting Germany’s interest in expanding cooperation in Nigeria’s energy sector.

Wadephul also commended the performance of the Nigeria-Germany Bi-National Commission, describing it as an effective mechanism for strengthening collaboration between both countries.

Beyond economic relations, the German foreign minister reiterated Berlin’s commitment to supporting regional stability, particularly through cooperation with ECOWAS.

He said Germany would continue to assist efforts aimed at tackling insecurity in West Africa, especially threats posed by terrorism and violent extremism in the Sahel region.

Wadephul expressed optimism about working closely with his Nigerian counterpart to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries.

The meeting comes amid renewed efforts by Nigeria to attract foreign investment, expand economic partnerships and deepen cooperation with international allies in areas including energy, technology, trade and security.

World.title: UI Appoints Prof. Olapegba As 14th Vice-Chancellor
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The Governing Council of the University of Ibadan (UI) has appointed Prof. Peter Olamakinde Olapegba as the institution’s 14th substantive vice-chancellor following a competitive selection process involving eight candidates.

The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Chief Adebisi Akande, made the announcement shortly after the council approved the recommendation of the Joint Council-Senate Selection Board.

Akande, while announcing the appointment, said the process of selecting a new vice-chancellor commenced in line with the provisions of the University Act ahead of the expiration of the tenure of the incumbent vice-chancellor on November 1, 2026.

He explained that s inviting applications for the position were published in three national newspapers in April 2026, attracting six applications from qualified candidates.

According to him, the governing council subsequently constituted a search team, as required by law, to identify other suitably qualified academics who had not initially applied for the position. The exercise yielded two additional applications, bringing the total number of candidates to eight.

The former Osun State governor disclosed that the council met with all eight candidates on Tuesday, July 21, for a rigorous assessment during which members independently evaluated and scored each candidate in accordance with approved guidelines.

Akande said the exercise produced five candidates who were shortlisted in order of merit for the final stage of the selection process.

He further explained that the Governing Council appointed two of its members to serve on the Joint Council-Senate Selection Board, while the University Senate had earlier elected two representatives to participate in the exercise.

He noted that the selection board interviewed the five shortlisted candidates on Wednesday before recommending Prof. Olapegba as the most suitable candidate for the office of vice-chancellor.

While describing the selection process as “thorough, transparent and highly competitive”, Akande said the Governing Council unanimously approved the recommendation of the Selection Board.

“It is, therefore, my pleasure to present to you the14th vice-chancellor of this great university, the University of Ibadan, Professor Peter Olamakinde Olapegba. We wish him success in his tenure,” Akande said.

Olapegba, who currently serves as the university’s deputy vice-chancellor (administration) and is a professor in the Department of Psychology, will succeed the incumbent vice-chancellor, whose tenure expires on November 1, 2026.

His appointment makes him the 14th substantive vice-chancellor of Nigeria’s premier university following a competitive selection process conducted in accordance with the university’s statutory provisions.

World.title: NDIC Begins Payment of Depositors of 46 Failed MfBs
World.content:
The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has begun paying insured deposits to customers of the 46 recently failed microfinance banks.

The NDIC Managing Director and Chief Executive, Mr Thompson Sunday, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Abuja.

The interview took place on the sidelines of the International Association of Deposit Insurers Africa Regional Committee meeting.

Sunday said the corporation was using the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System and customers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) for the payments.

He said NDIC had traced depositors’ alternative bank accounts and credited them directly without requiring physical visits.

He advised depositors without BVNs to visit the nearest NDIC zonal office for verification and payment processing.

“The CBN revoked the licences of the 46 microfinance banks on July 1, 2026,” he said.

He said NDIC automatically became the provisional liquidator after the revocation, in line with the law.

Sunday said the corporation had commenced payment of the insured maximum deposit of N2 million to eligible customers.

He explained that further payments would depend on the recovery of the failed banks’ assets and outstanding debts.

He said proceeds realised from recoveries would be distributed as liquidation dividends to eligible depositors.

Sunday cited Heritage Bank, Aso Savings and Union Homes as examples of NDIC’s prompt reimbursement efforts.

He said insured depositors of Heritage Bank were paid within four days of licence revocation.

He added that customers of Aso Savings and Union Homes received payments within 72 hours.

“The law allows us 30 days, but we are working to surpass our previous records,” he said.

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) revoked the banks’ licences for failing to meet regulatory requirements for continued operations.

The apex bank said the action was aimed at protecting depositors, strengthening financial stability and ensuring regulatory compliance. (NAN)

World.title: Olaopa Urges Support For Policy Institutes
World.content:
The Chairman, Federal Civil Service Commission ( FCSC), Prof. Tunji Olaopa, has urged support for development and policy institutes in the country.

Olaopa made the appeal when the President of the Chartered Institute of Development Studies and Administration of Nigeria ( CIDSA) , Dr Elijah O. Ogbuokiri , led a delegation of the institute to his office in Abuja on Wednesday.

According to him, such support has become necessary to break the trend of government depending on foreign policy bodies . He specifically decried a situation where in most cases, the most quoted statistics on development issues in Nigeria are from foreign institutions like the World Bank and International Monetary Fund .

Olaopa described CIDSAN as a relevant multi-disciplinary body concerned with policy and administration.

According to Olaopa, the institute is relevant in light of his experience as a bureaucrat in 27 years in the federal civil service where he was involved in strategic policy making and leading public and education reforms.

He said that in the course of these engagements, he observed a huge lacuna in terms of the quality of support and problem solving for the federal bureaucracy by policy institutes.

He disclosed that it was to fill this vacuum that he set up the Ibadan School of Government and Public Policy ( ISGPP) upon retirement before he left for the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies ( NIPSS).

He said that his experience at NIPSS confirmed what he observed earlier. He said that he observed that most of the institutions that contribute to policy making are faced with the same challenges in terms of capacity and funding.

Thus, for him, those in government who are involved in policy making owe the nation and government the responsibility of building national policy and development institutions through patronage. He said that these institutions need policy evangelists to deepen policy work to drive national projects.

According to him, this reliance on foreign policy bodies is seen in the adoption of best practices developed in socioeconomic contexts that are different from those of Nigeria.

But while acknowledging that there are some institutions making impact in terms of technical support in the private sector, he said that their theories of change are not largely applicable in the public sector.

He urged civil servants to invest in learning from policy institutes while they are in service. He said that while he was in service, he seized every opportunity available to learn from policy institutes locally and overseas.

Earlier, Dr Ogbuokiri said that he and his team were at the FCSC in order to forge a collaboration with the commission. He urged civil servants to join the institute and be trained as experts in different areas of development and policy .

World.title: Transcorp Hotels Grows H1 Profit, Posts ₦13.7bn PBT Despite Challenging Market
World.content:
Transcorp Hotels Plc, the hospitality subsidiary of Transnational Corporation Plc , has announced its unaudited results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by disciplined cost management and continued operational excellence despite moderated revenue.

The Company delivered ₦10.5 billion in profit after tax, a 21% increase from ₦8.7 billion in Q2 2025, while Profit Before Tax (PBT) increased by 12% to ₦13.7 billion from ₦12.2 billion in the same period in 2025.

According to key highlights in the report, revenue stood at ₦44.4 billion, compared to ₦46.9 billion in the second quarter of 2025, reflecting softer market demand in the company’s International Business segment. Despite this, Profit Before Tax increased by 12 per cent to ₦13.7 billion from ₦12.2 billion, while Profit After Tax rose by 21 per cent to ₦10.5 billion, compared to ₦8.7 billion in the corresponding period last year. The company’s Operating Expense Margin also improved by three percentage points, underscoring continued operational efficiency and prudent cost management.

These results validate Transcorp Hotels’ resilience and focus on operational excellence, cost efficiency, and customer-centric innovation, reinforcing its leadership in Nigeria’s hospitality sector.

Managing Director/CEO, Transcorp Hotels Plc, Uzoamaka Oshogwe commented:”Our Q2 2026 performance reflects the resilience of our business and the disciplined execution of our strategy in a dynamic operating environment. While market conditions remained challenging, we continued to deliver strong profitability by staying focused on operational excellence, commercial agility, and creating exceptional experiences for our guests.

We remain committed to strengthening our market leadership, investing strategically in our business, and delivering sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.”

Chief Finance Officer, Transcorp Hotels Plc, Oluwatobiloba Ojediran, added: “Our disciplined approach to cost management, revenue optimisation, and operational execution delivered a 12% increase in Profit Before Tax to ₦13.7 billion, alongside a 21% growth in Profit After Tax to ₦10.5 billion, compared with ₦8.7 billion in the corresponding period last year. These strong financial results reinforce the resilience of our business, provide a solid platform for sustainable growth, and position us to continue investing strategically while delivering long-term value for our shareholders.”

Beyond the numbers, Transcorp Hotels continues to strengthen its portfolio of iconic assets. Transcorp Hilton Abuja remains one of the Company’s flagship properties, while Transcorp Centre, one of West Africa’s largest purpose-built event and conference venues, is fast becoming a landmark for business, tourism, and world-class events in Nigeria. Since its launch, the venue has hosted several landmark gatherings, further cementing its position as a premier venue for high-profile corporate and social gatherings.

World.title: FG’ll Ensure Maritime Seminar Resolutions Are Translated to Policy, Legislation, Says SGF
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Federal Government on Wednesday pledged to ensure that resolutions from the 18th International Maritime Seminar for Judges are translated into policy, legislation, and institutional reforms.

The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, made the commitment in Abuja at the opening ceremony of the seminar organised by the Nigerian Shippers’ Council (NSC) in collaboration with the National Judicial Institute and the Nigerian Maritime Law Association.

Speaking as chairman of the occasion, Senator Akume stated that maritime justice is “not a sectoral concern but a national governance issue” that directly impacts trade, investment and the cost of living for Nigerians.

He noted that when a maritime claim is delayed in court, trade suffers, adding; “When a ship arrest is poorly executed, investor confidence falls. When cargo disputes go unresolved, the cost of essential imports rises — and ordinary Nigerians bear that cost.”

Akume explained that effective maritime commerce requires harmony among key agencies including the Nigerian Shippers’ Council, Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), Nigeria Port Authority (NPA) Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, and the Federal High Court.

He said the Office of the SGF would provide the coordinating platform to ensure data sharing, regulatory alignment, and follow-through on the seminar’s recommendations, noting that: “Where resolutions call for legislative review, we will engage the National Assembly and the Federal Ministry of Justice. Where they require ratification of international conventions, we will ensure executive attention.”

Akume commended the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, for declaring the seminar open, noting that a “strong, knowledgeable, and independent judiciary is not a complement to national development. It is a precondition for it”.

He also welcomed Chief Justices and senior judicial officers from Ghana, Sierra Leone, The Gambia, Kenya and Liberia, describing their presence as proof of trust in Nigeria’s commitment to regional judicial cooperation.

He expressed hope that the forum would accelerate the harmonisation of commercial and maritime laws in West Africa to boost intra-African shipping and trade.

He noted that a credible and efficient maritime justice system is “foundational” to attracting investors and positioning Nigeria as a competitive hub in global shipping even as he praised the Nigerian Shippers’ Council for sustaining the seminar since 1995, calling the 31-year milestone “a legacy worthy of national commendation”.

Linking the seminar to the President Bola Tinubu administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda, Akume said the Blue Economy has been made a strategic priority to drive jobs, investment and economic diversification, and called on inter-agency synergy drive to unlock the sector.

He equally acknowledged the National Judicial Institute (NJI) and the Nigerian Maritime Law Association for their enduring partnership, saying the strength of the seminar lies in collaboration between regulatory, judicial and professional institutions.

Delivering his keynote address, the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, urged the judiciary to prepare for a new generation of maritime disputes arising from autonomous ships, digital shipping and the global transition to cleaner maritime transport.

He stated that the rapid evolution of maritime technology was creating unprecedented legal questions around liability, navigational responsibility, insurance, collision regulations and the allocation of responsibility when autonomous vessels or their systems fail.

He added that the annual seminar has become one of Nigeria’s foremost platforms for strengthening maritime students, enhancing judicial capacity, and promoting excellence in the administration of judges within Nigeria’s marine and marine economy sector.

According to Oyetola, “The enduring motto of this seminar, ‘Advancing Maritime Justice, Strengthening Global Trade,’ aptly captures the indispensable relationship between a sound legal system and a prosperous maritime economy. Maritime commerce flourishes where the rule of law is respected, contractual obligations are enforced, disputes are resolved fairly and expeditiously, and judicial decisions inspire confidence among investors and trading partners.”

Also speaking, the CJN, Justice Kekere-Ekun, said the maritime sector serves as a vital channel for the movement of goods and services, facilitates international trade, supports economic growth and contributes significantly to employment and national revenue.

The CJN further emphasised the importance of effective and prompt dispensation of admiralty justice, noting that maritime disputes often involve complex, time-sensitive and cross-border transactions.

She stressed that delays in resolving such disputes could disrupt commercial operations, increase costs, undermine investor confidence and affect the smooth functioning of the maritime industry.

She therefore underscored the need for a responsive, efficient and specialised system of admiralty justice capable of resolving maritime disputes in a timely and effective manner.

The three-day seminar is expected to address contemporary issues in admiralty law, port operations and dispute resolution, with participation from judges and maritime experts across Africa.

World.title: Nigerian Navy Hands Over Rescued Victims of Human Trafficking to NAPTIP
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy has handed over rescued victims of suspected human trafficking to the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), reinforcing inter-agency efforts to combat human trafficking, protect vulnerable persons, and ensure survivors receive the care, protection and support required for their rehabilitation and reintegration into society.

The Service also reaffirmed its commitment to tackling human trafficking and other transnational organised crimes through the successful handover of the two rescued victims to NAPTIP.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Nigerian Navy, Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the handover was carried out by Forward Operating Base (FOB) Badagry at the Agency’s Lagos Zonal Command in Ikeja, following the victims’ rescue during a targeted anti-human trafficking operation.

He said: “In line with the Harmonized Standard Operating Procedures (HSOP) for the handling of victims of trafficking, the rescued individuals were first taken to the Western Naval Command Maritime Crime Investigation Desk, where they underwent comprehensive documentation, biometric capture, and other necessary administrative procedures before being formally transferred to NAPTIP for rehabilitation, protection, and further investigation.”

Captain Folorunsho said the successful rescue and seamless handover underscored the Nigerian Navy’s unwavering commitment to safeguarding Nigeria’s maritime and territorial corridors from transnational organised crime while ensuring the protection and dignity of vulnerable persons.

“It also reflects the Service’s continued collaboration with relevant government agencies in dismantling human trafficking networks and strengthening Nigeria’s national security architecture,” he said.

The statement added that the Nigerian Navy remains resolute in sustaining intelligence-driven operations and inter-agency cooperation aimed at preventing human trafficking, disrupting criminal syndicates, and promoting a safe and secure maritime environment in support of national security objectives.

World.title: Mr and Mrs Beast? Who is YouTuber’s South African wife?
World.content:
Who is Mr Beast's South African wife, Thea Booysen? Images via Instagram

YouTuber and social media star Mr Beast – real name Jimmy Donaldson – has found his “Mrs” – a South African woman named Thea Booysen.

The couple married at a picturesque wedding in the British Virgin Islands last week.

MR BEAST WEDS MRS BEAST!

On their Instagram accounts, Mr Beast and Thea Booysen posted wedding pictures from their recent nuptials.



The couple tied the knot in an intimate wedding in front of 70 guests at Richard Branson’s private Necker Island.

The US content creator wore a black and white tuxedo, whilst his blonde bride was snapped in not one, but three wedding dresses at the celebration.

Mr Beast – the world’s richest YouTuber, who has half a billion subscribers – captioned the post: “I found Mrs Beast, and it was the best day of my life”.

His post received almost 7 million likes at the time of publishing.

WHO IS SOUTH AFRICA’S THEA BOOYSEN? AND WHERE DID THEY MEET?

Mr Beast’s new bride is South African content creator Thea Booysen.

The couple met in early 2022 when the YouTuber visited South Africa alongside content creators like Logan Paul and Casey Neistat.



Here’s what we know about Mrs Beast…

Thea was born and raised in Cape Town.

She is an avid gamer and has her own YouTube channel called TheaBeasty.

He is a Twitch streamer and esports commentator.

She studied law and psychology at Stellenbosch University. She later completed a master’s degree in Human Cognitive Neuropsychology at the University of Edinburgh.

Thea is also an avid writer and released her debut adult fiction novel, The Marked Children, in 2022.

World.title: ‘He’s like Pogba’: Ex-Tanzania coach hails Kaizer Chiefs’ new midfield signing
World.content:
Former Tanzania national team head coach Adel Amrouche has linked new Kaizer Chiefs signing Adolf Mtasingwa Bitegeko to French star Paul Pogba.



Bitegeko is yet to play for Amakhosi but his former coach believes the Soweto giants have signed a ‘baller’. The former Azam midfielder is Chiefs’ third signing of the season after Renaldo Leaner and Thabo Moloisane.

“He has good height, plays with simplicity and doesn’t complicate his life on the pitch,” Amrouche said as per GOAL.

“He can be even better if he finds an environment where he’s trusted and managed well.

“He’s like Pogba. Adolf has a nice passing range.”

Bitegeko’s former Azam FC teammate Prince Dube also shared his thoughts on what Kaizer Chiefs can expect from their new midfielder.

“He’s a typical defensive midfielder who sits in front of the defence and protects the back four well.



“I think he’ll fit in very well at Kaizer Chiefs.

“He needs to adjust because South African football is quicker, but his passing is very good,” Dube added.

Can the new Kaizer Chiefs midfielder deliver?

The 27-year-old midfielder has played for KR Reykjavik, Keflavik, and Volsungur IF, and also had brief spells in Norway and Finland.

He joined Azam in 2024 and immediately became one of the most sought after midfielder in Tanzania. At Amakhosi, he will have to fight Sibongiseni Mthwethwa and Siphesihle Ndlove for the number six position.

He might get his first run when Kaizer Chiefs play Scotland FC in the Toyota Cup this weekend.

Do you expect new Chiefs midfielder to dominate the midfield?

World.title: Zambia intercepts Somali migrants hidden under bags of rice
World.content:
Somali migrants were found hidden beneath bags of rice in a vehicle intercepted in Zambia. Image via Facebook/Kalemba

Seven Somali nationals were discovered concealed beneath bags of rice in a vehicle travelling towards Zimbabwe after Zambian authorities intercepted a suspected migrant smuggling operation during a routine inspection.



The Somali nationals are believed to have been travelling to South Africa via Zimbabwe, with the Chirundu One Stop Border Post serving as their intended crossing point into Zimbabwe.

The Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) said the seven men were found hidden in the rear cargo compartment of a Toyota Probox that had been stopped in Kapiri Mposhi.

Seven Somali migrants concealed beneath bags of rice

According to the ZRA, officers became suspicious after stopping the vehicle during a routine enforcement operation.

A search of the vehicle revealed seven Somali nationals hidden beneath bags of rice and other goods in the cargo area.

Images released by the authority showed officers unloading sacks of rice before the migrants emerged from the cramped compartment where they had allegedly been concealed for the journey.

The Zambian driver of the vehicle was immediately detained.



Driver and migrants handed over to immigration officials

The ZRA said both the driver and the seven Somali nationals were handed over to Zambia’s Department of Immigration for profiling and further investigations.

According to the ZRA, the driver and the seven Somali nationals were transferred to the Department of Immigration for profiling and possible legal action in line with the Immigration and Deportation Act.

Authorities have not disclosed where the migrants began their journey or whether Zimbabwe was their final destination.

The Chirundu One Stop Border Post serves as one of Southern Africa’s busiest trade and transport corridors, linking Zambia with Zimbabwe and connecting traffic moving further south through the region.

Zambian authorities reiterate warning on law enforcement

In a separate enforcement operation, the ZRA also impounded a vehicle that had remained in Zambia after its temporary import permit expired.

According to the authority, the vehicle entered Zambia through the Kasumbalesa Border Post in December 2025 but was never re-exported after the permit lapsed, breaching the country’s customs regulations.



The revenue authority used the incidents to remind motorists, importers and transport operators to comply with immigration and customs laws.

It warned that violations could result in enforcement action, including the seizure of vehicles and goods, as authorities continue to tighten compliance along Zambia’s border routes.

World.title: Confirmed: Orlando Pirates starting XI vs La Palmas
World.content:
Orlando Pirates are back in action just 24 hours after their 3-2 defeat to Al-Ittihad. Tonight they take on Spanish Segunda División side UD Las Palmas at the Marbella Football Center at 19:00.

The Betway Premiership giants are using their pre-season tour to build match fitness. Additionally, some tactical understanding ahead of the new domestic season and the CAF Champions League campaign.

CONFIRMED STARTING LINE UP: Dladla, Chabatsane, Zulu, Rapoo, Lungu, Mthiyane, Dansin (C), Mmolai, Msendami, Padime, Mbuthuma.



Substitutes: Monyepoa (GK), Xoki, Derbyshire, Mariko, De Jong, Masilela, Radiopane.

ORLANDO PIRATES AIM TO BOUNCE BACK

The Buccaneers have enjoyed a competitive tour of Spain so far. The Buccaneers opened with a 1-1 draw against Córdoba CF, with youngster Boitumelo Radiopane finding the back of the net.

They followed that up with an impressive 2-1 comeback victory over Cádiz CF, thanks to goals from Thalente Mbatha and Daniel Msendami.

However, Orlando Pirates suffered their first defeat of the tour on Tuesday after going down 3-2 to Saudi Pro League giants Al-Ittihad. Despite dominating possession for long spells, defensive lapses proved costly as Ouaddou’s side conceded three goals.

UD LAS PALMAS PROVIDE ANOTHER TOUGH EXAMINATION

UD Las Palmas are expected to provide another stern test for Orlando Pirates as they continue preparations for the new season. The Spanish outfit are also under new leadership with Rubén de la Barrera taking charge after the club narrowly missed out on promotion to LaLiga last season.

The two teams have previously met in pre-season, playing out a goalless draw in a tightly contested encounter in 2025.



With another demanding fixture on the schedule, Ouaddou will be looking for an improved defensive display while continuing to assess his squad ahead of the Betway Premiership opener. The match will be broadcast live on SuperSport 209 and streamed on Pirates TV on YouTube.

World.title: Consumer profile: Who is South Africa’s electric car buyer?
World.content:
South Africans have to contend with rising fuel prices and uncertainty surrounding when these surging costs will end. Waiting in the wings are electric vehicles (EVs). But who’s buying them when the country doesn’t have an elaborate charging network?

The Niche Buyer Interested in Electric Cars

China, the world’s largest EV market, has over 20 million charging points. The United States, the second largest market for EVs, has 250 000 charging points. There are roughly 300 charging points in South Africa.

Yet there are headlines that consumers are buying electric vehicles, spurred by the rising cost of petrol and less load-shedding.



Who’s buying these cars when there are so few charging points?

Alan Quinn, Chief Product and Innovation Officer at cars.co.za, answered that question in an interview with Jeremy Magg.

Quinn pointed out a growing niche that would be persuaded to buy an electric vehicle despite the challenges presented by a limited charging network.

“I don’t know where my nearest EV charger is and most people don’t,” Quinn admitted.

He added that trying to sell electric cars “based on charging networks and… range anxiety” isn’t viable in 2026 and wouldn’t be “for a couple of years.”

However, he shared there was a market segment that could find the car useful.



“I think there’s other niches and that’s where we’re seeing the growth coming,” he said, referencing two-car households.

“I might want one car to drive to Dalstrom at the weekend, but I don’t need two cars to drive to Dalstrom,” he expressed.

Quinn pointed to anecdotal evidence that some buyers use electric vehicles as a daily driver. Referencing a friend who’s “seeing a lot of Dolphin Surfs sitting about,” Quinn stated, “people are using them for their dailies. And so that is a niche and not a small niche.”

But he added that other niches could embrace the electric vehicle while there wasn’t a large charging network: fleets.

“Now, because of the petrol price, because of the operating costs, because of model availability and manufacturers buying it,” an executive might be persuaded to choose electric for their fleet, he stated.

“Those cars have defined radiuses. They come back to home base every night.”

Therein lies the niche that could increase demand for electric vehicles.

“You will start to grow a demand. And those niches will gradually expand,” Quinn suggested.

How Buyers will Fund their Electric Car Purchase

To assist the potential demand, Quinn discussed the ABSA partnership with BYD and the launch of BYD finance.

He noted the partnership used a Guaranteed Future Value (GFV) model, which operates much like a rental contract.

“In a rental contract, you don’t worry about what the vehicle is worth in the future,” he stated.

Quinn also highlighted the differences between a GFV contract and the typical car finance contract. In a GFV contract, consumers buy their own insurance and pay for their tyres.

“Other than that, you take the keys, you drive around a few years, you give them back like a rental contract. Now, what that takes away is anxiety over what this car is going to be worth in three years’ time. And for EVs, that’s a real anxiety,” Quinn concluded.

Sales Data for Electric Vehicles

According to data from Naamsa, South Africa’s electric vehicle market grew to 18 times its size between 2021 and 2025. Sales of EVs, which include plug-in hybrids, traditional hybrids, and battery electric vehicles, grew from a total of 896 sales in 2021 to 16 716 in 2025.

That still makes up less than 3% of new vehicle purchases in South Africa.

However, much of this data predates the entry of more affordable options like the BYD Dolphin Surf and Geely E2, which brought the cost of EVs closer to R300 000.

Affordable electric vehicles could make EVs more appealing to South Africans battling rampant fuel prices.

World.title: DA to ask Public Protector to probe Gayton McKenzie over R110m
World.content:
DA Sport, Arts and Culture spokesperson Leah Potgieter (left) and deputy spokesperson Joe McGluwa will lead the party's submission of a complaint against Minister Gayton McKenzie to the Public Protector. Image: People's Assembly

The Democratic Alliance (DA) will ask the Public Protector to investigate Sport, Arts and Culture Minister Gayton McKenzie over allegations involving nearly R110 million in public funds.



The party will submit a dossier on Thursday. It alleges breaches of the Executive Members’ Ethics Act, misuse of public money and a jobs-for-pals scheme benefiting the Patriotic Alliance.

It also wants the Public Protector to examine McKenzie’s FIFA World Cup trips.

DA Sport, Arts and Culture spokesperson Leah Potgieter and her deputy Joe McGluwa will lead the submission in Pretoria.

DA seeks investigation

The DA says its complaint sets out evidence of multiple alleged breaches of the minister’s legal and ethical obligations.

It claims departmental decisions benefited political allies and calls for a full investigation into the expenditure.

The party is expected to release more details after submitting the complaint.



Pressure grows over FIFA spending

The latest move follows renewed scrutiny of the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture’s R31.95 million FIFA Club World Cup expenditure.

As previously reported by The South African, opposition parties questioned whether the spending delivered value for taxpayers and called for greater accountability.

McKenzie rejected the criticism. He said the investment would support football development, create opportunities for players and administrators, and strengthen South Africa’s international sporting partnerships.

He also maintained that the expenditure complied with the department’s mandate.

Thursday’s complaint signals a further escalation in the political battle over the department’s spending.

What happens next?

The Public Protector will consider the submission before deciding whether to launch an investigation.



The DA is scheduled to lodge its complaint at 11:00 on Thursday, 23 July.

The South African has requested comment from McKenzie’s office. This article will be updated once a response is received.

World.title: Unclaimed Daily Lotto prize still waiting for a winner in East London
World.content:
An unclaimed Daily Lotto prize worth R55 012 is waiting to be claimed in East London. The person who won it appears to have no idea he – or she – has done so.



Somewhere in the city, someone won the Daily Lotto, but didn’t check their numbers.

The unclaimed Daily Lotto prize nobody has come forward for

Someone bought a Daily Lotto ticket in East London in early October last year that matched numbers drawn to win R55 012.

Months later, nobody has claimed it.

National Lottery rules give winners 365 days to come forward to collect their prize. That puts the deadline at 2 October 2026.

While it’s a modest win compared to the multimillion rand jackpots that usually make headlines, that may be exactly why it has slipped through the cracks.

Smaller wins are often the easiest to forget, especially when they come from a game played every single day.



What happens if the deadline passes

If the ticket is not claimed by 2 October 2026, the National Lottery Distribution Trust Fund receives the money instead.

From there, it gets redirected toward charities, sport, arts and community development rather than the player who actually won it.

You can read more about how unclaimed prizes are handled in our earlier report on the R257 million currently sitting unclaimed nationwide.

For the official rules on claiming a prize, the National Lottery’s claims page has the full process laid out.

Sizekhaya is still processing old tickets

Sizekhaya, which took over as the National Lottery’s operator on 1 June 2026, continues to process claims on outstanding ITHUBA-era tickets like this one.

Players do not need to worry about the change in operator affecting a valid claim.



I always say the same thing when these stories come up: an unclaimed Daily Lotto prize of R55 012 might not make front page news, but it is still real money sitting forgotten in someone’s ticket drawer.

Could this unclaimed Daily Lotto prize be yours?

Tell us in the comments, Mzansi …

World.title: British-Zimbabwean fugitive Tshuma drops bail bid, extradition looms
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - British-Zimbabwean national Ndodana Tshuma, wanted for the murders of his wife and two daughters in the UK, remains behind bars in Johannesburg.

He has withdrawn his bail application as police finalise their investigations.

Tshuma is facing extradition as well as charges related to the possession of an unlicensed firearm.

The state’s case is still missing evidence, including a ballistic report and extradition papers.

Since his first appearance last week, the State has sought to verify Tshuma's legal immigration status within the country.

WATCH: eNCA outside Ndodana Tshuma's home in UK

Authorities have classified him as a fugitive after he ran away from the UK to evade arrest.

UK authorities have confirmed that the three victims, his wife and two young daughters, died of blunt-force trauma after their bodies were found in their Bedford home.

Reports have also suggested that Tshuma's wife was in the process of divorcing him.

Tshuma must serve his time in South Africa for the unlicensed firearm charge first, meaning it could still take weeks or months before he is extradited to the United Kingdom.

eNCA's Bafedile Moerane has more details in the video above.

World.title: Motsepe rules out Presidential bid
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South African mining magnate Patrice Motsepe on Wednesday ruled out a future in politics, dismissing speculation that he could one day run for the country's Presidency.

The 64-year-old billionaire and head of African football has been repeatedly mentioned in the South African media as a potential successor to his brother-in-law, President Cyril Ramaphosa, whose second and final term ends in 2029.

"South Africa does not need me to go into politics," Motsepe told reporters in Johannesburg.

"There are many very capable and good leaders in this country," he said.

Motsepe also ruled out a bid to succeed Gianni Infantino as FIFA chief, saying he remained focused on his role at the helm of the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

"I have no desire or ambition to be president of FIFA. That doesn't excite me," he said. Motsepe's current CAF term runs until 2029.

South Africa's succession debate has intensified within the governing ANC as Ramaphosa navigates a turbulent second term, after the party's worst electoral performance forced it into an uneasy coalition government.

The President has also faced renewed pressure over a cash-heist scandal, in which $580,000 was stolen from his private game farm.

The ANC blocked impeachment proceedings against Ramaphosa over the scandal in 2022, but the Constitutional Court revived the process in May.

Motsepe brushed aside suggestions that he could be drawn into the contest to succeed Ramaphosa.

"The only problem I have is I'm not part of any group," he said.

"That's why even some of my friends say things which are not flattering, because somebody said to them that somebody might persuade me to change my view."

In December, Motsepe attended the ANC's national general council meeting, where some delegates wore T-shirts emblazoned with the slogan "PM27", a reference to a possible Presidential bid in 2027. A lobbying website bearing the same name has also been launched.

He founded and owns mining company African Rainbow Minerals and is Africa's eighth richest person, with a personal wealth estimated at $4.3 billion, according to Forbes magazine.

In 2012, Motsepe made the Forbes billionaire list.

He also owns CAF Champions League winners Mamelodi Sundowns.

World.title: Legal net tightens as state combines criminal cases against Nkosi
World.content:
PRETORIA - Days after appearing at the Thohoyandou Magistrates' Court, suspended Organised Crime Unit policeman Sergeant Fannie Nkosi is back at the Pretoria North Magistrates' Court.

The state has combined his Limpopo criminal charges with his existing Pretoria cases into a single prosecution.

The state is ready to go to trial against the suspended Organised Crime Unit officer.

He faces multiple charges including theft, fraud and defeating the ends of justice.

Some of the allegations stem from evidence before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

READ: Cop in the dock: State ready to take Fannie Nkosi to trial

And this relates to a case in 2022, where Nkosi allegedly removed a docket and exhibits under false pretences from the Thohoyandou Police Station.

He also faces charges for possessing explosives and failing to safeguard weapons.

These arise from his April arrest, where police uncovered hidden cash and stolen dockets at his home.

Nkosi has also been accused of acting as a middleman, helping drug cartels infiltrate law enforcement.

In what's been a double blow for Nkosi, he remains behind bars after being denied bail by both the Pretoria North Magistrate's Court and the High Court in Pretoria.

His case has now been transferred to Regional Court 1, where he will stand trial.

eNCA's Manqoba Mchunu reports in the video above.

World.title: Nkabinde Inquiry panel clears Andrew Chauke
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg Director of Public Prosecutions, Andrew Chauke, has been cleared and found fit to remain in office.

Former National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) head Advocate Shamila Batohi had accused Chauke of wrongly charging former KZN Hawks head Johan Booysen and members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit with racketeering.

READ | Advocate Andrew Chauke under intense scrutiny at Nkabinde inquiry

She had also questioned his decision not to prosecute former crime intelligence head Richard Mdluli.

President Cyril Ramaphosa appointed the Nkabinde Inquiry to investigate whether or not Chauke was fit to hold office.

He has been on paid suspension since July 2025.

World.title: Senior crime intelligence officer Ismail Dawood granted bail
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Senior crime intelligence officer Ismail Dawood has been granted bail.



The High Court in Johannesburg granted Dawood R10,000 bail.



Dawood faces charges of extortion and assault.



He is expected back at the Johannesburg Magistrate's Court on Friday.

READ: 'It's ridiculous': Defence slams delay in Dawood extortion case



Dawood has been barred from contacting key state witnesses.

The National Prosecution Authority has responded to Dawood being granted bail.



"The State subsequently succeeded in verifying the accused’s residential address," the NPA said.



"Following the verification, the defence approached the High Court on an urgent basis seeking the accused’s release on bail. The State did not oppose the application, and the High Court granted bail accordingly.

"It is alleged that in December 2023, the accused and the complainant met in Hillbrow, Johannesburg, where Dawood allegedly assaulted the complainant during the meeting.

"The State further alleges that the accused demanded money from the complainant, which was subsequently paid at his instance. It is further alleged that the accused thereafter continued to make additional demands for money from the complainant.

"The NPA will continue to present all relevant evidence before the court and remains committed to ensuring that the matter is prosecuted fairly and in accordance with the law."

World.title: Big money boost for Women's AFCON as CAF injects millions
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Confederation of African Football has increased the Women's Africa Cup of Nations prize money.



The winners of the competition are set to walk away with $2-million (R33-million).



That is 100% more than what Nigeria pocketed when they defeated Morocco in the final a year ago.



The total purse is up by 67% for the tournament, which kicks off on Sunday.

World.title: Cop in the dock:  State ready to take Fannie Nkosi to trial
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The state said it's ready to go to trial against suspended Organised Crime Unit officer Fannie Nkosi.



Both his Gauteng and Limpopo criminal cases will be heard together.



Nkosi appeared in the Pretoria North Magistrate's Court.

READ: Fannie Nkosi back in court after cases centralised



He faces charges of theft, fraud and defeating the ends of justice and has been accused of helping criminal syndicates infiltrate law enforcement.



The matter has been postponed to 19 August.

World.title: More South Africans struggle under debt pressure
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The rising cost of living is making it harder for many South Africans to make ends meet.



From food and fuel to electricity bills, everyday expenses are putting household budgets under pressure.



This has left more consumers reliant on debt to get through the month.



DebtBusters' latest Money Stress Tracker shows that 53% of consumers now spend more than 40% of their take-home pay on debt repayments.



More than a third spend half or more of their income servicing debt, well above the recommended threshold.



The survey also found that financial stress has intensified, with concerns shifting from debt and interest rates to the rising cost of living.

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).
