World.title: EIS uses €6.5 million communications budget to target 20 countries
World.content:
Ursel Velve, head of the Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS), says the agency aims to justify every euro of its communications budget, calling the spending essential for promoting Estonia abroad.

When Velve took over leadership of EIS about a year ago, she examined the foundation's marketing and communication activities in detail. Previously, each EIS department had its own marketing and communication team, and when information about all their activities was compiled, the list contained about three hundred items.

EIS merged these teams, and at the beginning of 2026 the number of employees there was reduced from 70 to 39. "We have critically reviewed all the activities we do and all the people, so that everyone contributes to the maximum," Velve said.

Velve said that when she started, she questioned above all those EIS communication expenses related to conferences or events aimed at small groups — events similar to those organized by the private sector — where costs were quite high while the value gained for the state was questionable.

Although public‑sector institutions employ a large number of communication staff, the state is paying increasingly large sums to private PR firms. EIS is among the biggest user of PR firms, despite having 39 employees working in marketing and communication.

According to Velve, the EIS communication budget this year is 6.5 million euros, divided across 20 countries in five fields: export, investment, growth of the start‑up community, e‑residency and tourism. Therefore, Velve noted, the amount per country and field is very small.

She gave an example from her previous experience working at a large electronics company, where the marketing and communication budget was about 2 percent of turnover — 3 million euros per year. "If a single product‑group company in small Estonia markets with 3 million, then our 6.5 million to make Estonia visible globally is still a very small amount."

She said that of the 39‑member EIS communication and marketing team, only three work on domestic communication, while the rest work outward toward 20 countries.

"The issue is that there are not many specialists or agencies in Estonia that truly have a strong international contact network in foreign markets. For example, last year we helped the EIS carry out a project aimed at supporting Estonian companies in export markets. To do such work, you need knowledge, experience and contacts in countries such as South Korea, the United States, Japan, Germany and many others," said Miltton New Nordics CEO Annika Arras.

"If we consider that we have large countries — the United Kingdom, Germany, Finland, Sweden, Singapore, South Korea and others — then inevitably each country has its own cultural differences and channels. On our own we simply cannot grasp what is most effective in a specific country," Velve explained.

Therefore, local partners must be involved.

"For example, there was a defense‑industry fair in Poland, where we took Estonian companies. Before and after the fair we did a lot of communication, which resulted in a defense‑industry media trip to Estonia that brought us 23 million contacts through coverage. Through this, cooperation between Estonian and Polish defense‑industry companies significantly intensified," Velve noted. "On one hand, the sums may seem large, but considering what it brings back to Estonia, it is certainly a worthwhile investment."

EIS has discussed with Estonian ministries, the Government Office and business associations how to organize Estonia's international marketing, and everyone says that marketing Estonia is extremely important, Velve said. "No one else in Estonia does it, so EIS must continue."

EIS is also involved, together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications, in organizing 2027 Ukraine reconstruction conference in Tallinn. "There we need good project‑based people who can bring defense‑industry companies from across the Nordic region to Estonia."

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: Ukraine’s new army chief: who is Mykhailo Drapaty?
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky has announced Mykhailo Drapaty as the country’s new commander-in-chief, following a political crisis triggered by Zelensky’s surprise ousting of a young modernising defence minister.

The 43-year-old Drapaty replaces Oleksandr Syrsky, 60, an accomplished military strategist but who was long criticised for Soviet-style practices and not caring about human losses.

Here is what we know about Drapaty.

– Fighting Russian separatists –

Drapaty is a career military officer trained exclusively inside Ukraine’s independent, post-Soviet system.

He began as a lieutenant and rose through the ranks, shooting to nationwide fame during the war with Russia-backed separatists in 2014.

In a video which went viral, he commanded an infantry vehicle as it smashed through a makeshift barricade set up by pro-Moscow forces in the southern city of Mariupol.

Recalling the incident in an interview with Ukrainian media, Drapaty said his driver asked: “Major, there are barricades ahead. What do we do?”

“I said, ‘Dima, step on the gas'”.

The vehicle, with the blue-and-yellow Ukrainian flag affixed to its top, then smashes through the tyre-and-barricade wall, leaping into the air and speeding on.

During the fight with Moscow-backed rebels, Drapaty is also credited with re-capturing several settlements from Russian control and then saving his unit from being encircled.

Drapaty has a wife and kids, Ukrainian media reported.

– Backing army ‘transformation’ –

Drapaty is seen as a consensus candidate and popular choice.

He enjoys a good reputation within the military, and protesters calling for his predecessor’s removal often chanted his name as their preferred replacement.

Despite being well-known, he has kept a low profile and only rarely given interviews — in contrast with many other Ukrainian commanders.

After a string of Russian attacks on Ukrainian training grounds, he resigned from his position as ground forces commander in June 2025 — a move that set him apart as commander willing to take responsibility for mistakes.

“If we fail to draw conclusions, to change our attitude toward service, to acknowledge our mistakes, we are doomed,” he said at the time.

“That episode illustrates his decisiveness and strong ethical standards,” political commentator Volodymyr Fesenko told AFP on Wednesday.

Drapaty was immediately moved to become head of Ukraine’s joint forces command, from where he pushed for reforms inside the system.

After the dismissal of moderniser Fedorov last week, he said the “transformation” of the army must continue.

“When the right decision has to be implemented in spite of the system, rather than because of it, it means that the system itself needs to change,” he said in a rare public intervention.

“The army needs new rules,” he added.

– Hailed as ‘fresh air’ –

His nomination was hailed by many inside and outside the army.

The appointment is “wonderful news”, said Sergiy Prytula, the head of one of Ukraine’s biggest charities supporting the military.

“This is a breath of fresh air and a new hope in the struggle of free people for freedom and justice,” the ousted defence minister Fedorov, an ally, said on social media.

In Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the change would not impact the course of the war.

“I don’t think this will lead to any changes on the front lines,” he told reporters, adding that Moscow intends to continue pressing on with its almost four-and-a-half-year offensive.

– Facing a ‘very difficult time’ –

Despite Ukraine being in one of its best positions on the front line in months, Drapaty faces serious challenges.

The army has been blighted by several scandals — particularly over an unpopular mobilisation drive, the treatment of conscripts and reports of widespread absenteeism and equipment shortages in some units.

“The new Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine will have a very difficult time. Much harder than he imagines,” former army chief Valery Zaluzhny — removed in 2024 — said.

The public row over the last week has exposed hidden divisions within Ukraine’s military and political leadership.

His appointment, seen as an attempt to bridge the divide, carries heavy expectations.

“Appointments made against a backdrop of social turmoil always come with many pitfalls,” said Prytula, adding that Drapaty now faces “inflated expectations”.

World.title: Iraq signs $200 billion in deals with US energy companies
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that the deals struck with US energy corporations during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States are estimated at $200 billion.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the new agreements will raise Iraq’s oil production capacity, create job opportunities, and help the country achieve self-sufficiency in gas by 2030, according to the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The deals include agreements with HKN Energy, Chevron, and Halliburton to develop the oilfields of Hamrin, West Qurna-2, Nasiriyah, Balad, Bin Omar, and Sindbad, as well as an agreement with Syria to construct the Haditha-Baniyas oil pipeline.

Khudair noted that Iraq’s current oil production capacity is 4.8 million barrels per day, but the government is in serious discussions with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to increase oil exports.

Just like most other oil producers, Iraq has to face the issue of how to attract investments and increase production under the restrictions imposed by OPEC.

Despite having some of the world’s greatest crude oil reserves, ongoing production constraints impede Iraq’s efforts to generate revenues needed to support its growing population.

World.title: Italian FA chief says in touch with Guardiola over coaching vacancy
World.content:
Rome – The head of Italy’s football federation has confirmed he held discussions with legendary coach Pep Guardiola over the vacancy at the Italian national side but added he was “not sure that this will come about”.

Giovanni Malago revealed the talks had taken place in an interview with the website Cronache di Spogliatoio (Dressing Room Chronicles) published on Wednesday.

Asked whether the budget for the coach’s salary could be increased in the case of Guardiola, he said: “Yes, and that is the exception for obvious reasons”.

“I won’t go into detail here but it’s not sure that this will come about.

“However, I still believe it was the right thing to do. It was important to open a dialogue and keep it alive,” he added.

Guardiola has first hand knowledge of Italian football having played for Brescia and AS Roma (2001-03).

Already at a low ebb, Italian football was sent into a tailspin in March after the men’s national team failed for a third consecutive time to qualify for the World Cup.

Italy has won four World Cups.

Guardiola, 55, stepped down at Manchester City at the end of last season after winning six Premier League titles and the Champions League in his glittering decade at the Etihad Stadium.

According to Italian media reports, former Italy internationals Andrea Pirlo and Roberto Mancini — who guided the Azzurri to the Euro 2020 title — are also being considered as candidates to coach the national team, which faces Belgium on September 25 in the Nations League.

World.title: Cooler inflation hands new UK PM Burnham an early boost
World.content:
London – Britain’s annual inflation rate fell more than expected in June, driven by lower fuel prices, official data showed Wednesday, in a boost to new Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s cost-of-living push.

The Consumer Prices Index rose by 2.6 percent in the 12 months to June, down from 2.8 percent in May, the Office for National Statistics said in a statement.

Analysts’ consensus forecast had been for a slowdown to 2.7 percent last month.

Much of the fall was a result of petrol and diesel prices easing as crude prices tumbled in the wake of a ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

However, analysts expect the inflation dip to be short-lived as fresh fighting in the Middle East this month led to the collapse of a preliminary peace deal, pushing oil prices back up.

Burnham, who became prime minister on Monday, has pledged to ease cost-of-living pressures, unveiling a tax cut on household electricity prices and a £2 ($2.70) cap on single bus fares in his first days in the job.

“Falling inflation is news families want to hear but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need,” said newly appointed finance minister John Healey.

“We have chosen to focus on the cost of living in our first week, signalling that concern for working people will be at the heart of everything we do,” he added.

– ‘Higher inflation still coming’ –

Burnham announced that value-added tax (VAT) would be taken off electricity bills from October in a policy costing the Labour government about £850 million in the current UK financial year.

The measure’s start date coincides with an expected rise in the UK energy regulator’s price cap on electricity and gas bills, a consequence of the ongoing US-Iran war that will likely spur inflation.

“Higher inflation is still coming,” said Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics.

“The lagged effect from high energy prices will probably lift inflation above 3.0 percent in September and to about 3.5 percent early next year,” he said.

Higher inflation meanwhile risks hikes to UK interest rates, analysts said.

The new PM has said he wishes to ease pressure also on small businesses, hit by the previous Labour administration’s tax hikes.

At the same time, Burnham has pledged to respect the strict fiscal discipline seen under his predecessor Keir Starmer, whereby the government balances tax receipts with day-to-day state spending.

Official data Tuesday showed UK government borrowing dropped more than expected in June, handing a boost Healey, who replaced Rachel Reeves as chancellor of the exchequer.

“While the general trend in the data is encouraging… the latest flare up in US-Iran tensions and the spike in oil prices means that it is unlikely to last, regardless of the cost-of-living measures deployed by the Burnham administration,” said Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury.

Burnham’s long-term goal is a “reindustrialisation” of Britain and mass building of municipal housing.

World.title: Iraq Oil Minister: $200B U.S. energy deals to boost crude output and gas by 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Minister of Oil, Basim Mohammed Khudair, announced on Tuesday that the federal government is advancing a clear strategic roadmap to comprehensively expand the nation’s energy infrastructure.

Speaking during an interview on the official Al-Iraqiya News channel, the Minister confirmed that the agreements finalized during Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s official visit to Washington will significantly boost total crude reserves, increase daily production, and generate extensive employment and technical training opportunities across the country.

Khudair revealed that the total estimated value of the energy contracts, strategic agreements, and memorandums of understanding executed during the U.S. summit reaches approximately $200 billion, emphasizing that the active presence of top American energy firms sends a strong message of market confidence to international investors.

Key Highlights from the Washington Energy Portfolio

HKN Energy Deal: Strategic development agreement signed to expand production at the Hamrin oil field.

Chevron Expansion: Operations and development agreements covering West Qurna 2, as well as the Nasiriya and Balad fields.

Halliburton Integrated Management: Comprehensive field management pacts secured for the Bin Umar and Sindibad fields.

Syrian Export Corridor: A major cross-border pipeline agreement signed with Syria to construct and reactivate the strategic Haditha–Baniyas pipeline.

World.title: Drone-assisted cross-border drug smuggling surges since 2021, Punjab worst hit: Government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The home ministry on Wednesday said drone-assisted, cross-border drug trafficking has risen exponentially since 2021, with Punjab being the most affected state, accounting for 298 of the 305 countrywide drone-related drug trafficking incidents last year.

Replying to a question in the Rajya Sabha, junior home minister Nityanand Rai said nearly 460 kg of narcotic drugs, including 448 kg of heroin, 9 kg of methamphetamine and 3 kg of opium was seized in actions against drone-assisted trafficking.

âTrends of cross border narcotics infiltration reveal that drug trafficking syndicates operating across the border have increasingly been employing sophisticated methods such as drones, GPS-enabled consignments, encrypted communications and local receiver networks to infiltrate heroin, methamphetamine, arms and ammunition into India,â Rai informed the Rajya Sabha.

World.title: 6.7 crore saplings planted by CAPFs in last 5 years: MHA tells Parliament
World.content: NEW DELHI: The Central armed police forces (CAPFs) have planted nearly 6.7 crore saplings in the last five years as part of a countrywide plantation drive, the home ministry told the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday.Junior home minister Nityanand Rai, in reply to a written question, shared that the seven CAPFs -- CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, NSG, SSB and Assam Rifles -- also developed a total 3,212 nurseries between 2020 and 2025 and set up and dedicated 1,995 âvatikasâ to martyrs between 2020 and 2024.A statewide distribution of the 6.9 crore saplings planted by the Central paramilitary forces in the last five years, shows north-eastern states at the top of the table. While Manipur saw the plantation of 64.8 lakh saplings, 61.2 lakh were planted in Nagaland and 59.6 lakh in Assam.CRPF and BSF, between themselves, developed 69% of the nurseries developed by the CAPFs in the last five years, according to data shared by Rai. ITBP led in development of vatikas, having set up 763 in the period 2020 to 2024.

World.title: 37,164 killed on 6,358 ‘black corridors’ of NHs in 3 yrs: Road ministry
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt has identified 6,358 âblack corridorsâ on NH network during 2023-25, which recorded 37,164 deaths, as per road transport ministry. The maximum such black corridors were in Tamil Nadu (958), followed by UP (671) and Karnataka (607).

Among districts, Viluppuram in Tamil Nadu had a maximum of 70 such corridors.

Unlike isolated black spots, these corridors are continuous stretches of NH that have recorded a higher number of fatal and grievous road crashes. The identification is expected to help authorities prioritise engineering interventions and improve

outcomes, officials said.

The road transport ministry informed the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday that black corridors have been identified based on the available crash data from Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e-DAR).

As per ministry data, Pune Rural district had 60 black corridors, followed by 52 in Purba Medinipur in West Bengal, 49 in Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu and 48 in Palakkad in Kerala.

Responding to a separate question, road transport minister Nitin Gadkari informed the Upper House that govt has adopted a phased roadmap for deployment of advanced traffic management systems (ATMS) across all four-lane and above NHs and expressways.





The roadmap includes establishment of local, regional, and national command and control centres for centralised monitoring, incident management, traffic analytics, and coordinated response.

In a written reply to another question on highway quality, the ministry said major deficiencies in NH stretches and bridges since March 2024 have been reported for 61 projects and stretches across the country. The deficiencies included collapse and defects in reinforced soil wall, girders, concrete panel, rutting and potholes. It said that 103 contractors and agencies have been blacklisted and penalised for poor quality work.

World.title: 58% of IRCTC booking requests were automated, access denied: Railways
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In the past six months, nearly 58% attempts to book train tickets online were by bots, not real people, the railway ministry informed Lok Sabha Wednesday. It said that on average 888 crore requests out of 1,538 crore in a month were bots, and those were flagged as automated requests and their access to the e-ticketing system was denied.

A bot is an automated software application that performs repetitive tasks over a network. It follows specific instructions to imitate human behaviour at a faster rate. In a written reply, railway minister Ashwni Vaishnaw said that such âspurious attemptsâ that were denied access to e-ticketing systems was the maximum in June â nearly 66% of the 1,912 crore requests by bots.

âBot manager in the system protects websites at its own cloud servers by using user behavioural analysis, bot signature/ pattern matching, and real-time risk scoring to instantly distinguish humans and bots and software,â an IRCTC official said.

Vaishnaw said the train ticket reservation system is robust and highly secure, and equipped with industry-standard, state-of-the-art cybersecurity controls while highlighting measures taken by railways to safeguard the system from cyber attacks, and prevent auto-filling of forms by hacking tools to curb fraud in Tatkal ticket bookings.

The minister said that multiple protective layers such as network firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, application delivery controllers and web application firewalls have been deployed to safeguard the system against cyber threats.





He added that little over three crore suspicious user IDs had been deactivated and 6.2 crore had been placed under revalidation during 2025-26 and 2026-27 (up to June 30).

The ministry said that 503 complaints have been lodged on the National Cyber Crime Portal for suspicious booking and 13,343 suspicious emails have been blocked in the past one-and-half years. In addition, since 2021, Railway Protection Force has arrested 22,676 touts and legal action has been taken.

World.title: Punjab's 'Business Class' programme helps over 20k student-led ventures garner Rs 90 cr revenue
World.content: NEW DELHI: Punjab's 'Business Class' programme, introduced under the state government's Sikhya Kranti initiative, has helped over 20,000 student-led ventures generate nearly Rs 90 crore in revenue within a year, Higher Education Minister Harjot Singh Bains said on Sunday.The programme, launched during the 2025-26 academic session, included a compulsory two-credit course for students pursuing B.Com, BBA, B.Tech and B.Voc courses, besides those studying in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and polytechnic colleges.According to the government, around 95,000 students from 925 higher and technical education institutions participated in the programme.Of these, 25,693 students started businesses, while 20,241 ventures generated nearly Rs 90 crore in revenue during the first year.Bains said the initiative aims to transform students from job seekers into entrepreneurs and employment generators."Our objective is not merely to award degrees but to nurture a generation of young innovators, entrepreneurs and job creators," he said in a statement.The minister further said the results demonstrate that young people can build businesses and contribute to the state's economy when provided with the right opportunities.Under Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann's leadership, Punjab's Sikhya Kranti is preparing youth "not just for the jobs of tomorrow, but to create tomorrow's opportunities," he said.The programme was implemented across 20 universities, 494 colleges, 320 ITIs and 91 polytechnic colleges.Unlike conventional classroom teaching, the course focuses on practical entrepreneurial skills, including identifying business opportunities, market validation, business setup, digital marketing, pricing, customer acquisition, financial planning and communication.The government said nearly 57,000 students, or about 60 per cent of participants, actively engaged in practical business activities during the academic session.Students launched ventures in sectors including e-commerce, food services, digital content creation, coding, graphic design, retail, beauty services, agriculture-based enterprises and handicrafts.Among the examples cited by the government were a matcha beverage startup by a Guru Nanak Dev University student, a digital career guidance platform developed by a student of Maharaja Ranjit Singh Punjab Technical University, an online jewellery business, a mushroom cultivation enterprise, a home-based nail art venture and an online electronics store.Encouraged by the programme's performance, vice-chancellors of universities across Punjab have recommended extending the course to all undergraduate programmes, including BA and BSc, from the 2026-27 academic session, the statement said.The government said the expansion is expected to equip a larger number of students with entrepreneurial skills alongside their regular academic studies.

World.title: Keep students focused on studies, away from protest calls: AIU to varsities
World.content:
AIU said prolonged protests could cause loss of academic time, disrupt preparation and create avoidable stress (representative image)

NEW DELHI: The Association of Indian Universities (AIU) has asked universities and higher education institutions to counsel students against staying away from classes to join protests over recent examination controversies, saying prolonged agitation comes at a âconsiderable costâ to their studies.In a letter to vice-chancellors and directors of member institutions, AIU president Vinay Kumar Pathak urged them to engage with students with empathy but ensure that their energies were not âdiverted by calls to protestâ.The July 21 letter comes amid continuing protests at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. Students and other protesters have demanded examination reforms, accountability for the leak and the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.âIn the wake of recent concerns surrounding the conduct of certain national-level examinations, a section of students on several campuses has been staying away from classes to take part in protests and agitations â at considerable cost to their own studies,â Pathak said.While acknowledging that studentsâ concerns deserved to be heard âwith empathy and respectâ, the AIU said prolonged protests could cause loss of academic time, disrupt preparation and create avoidable stress.âProlonged agitation exacts its heaviest price from the students themselves â in lost academic time, disrupted preparation and avoidable stress,â the letter said.The AIU argued that this cost was unnecessary as the government was committed to resolving the concerns and had conducted the recent NEET examination in a âtransparent and error-free mannerâ. The June 21 examination was held after the original May 3 test was cancelled following a question-paper leak.âI would, therefore, earnestly appeal to you to counsel our students â with patience, sensitivity and care for their future â to remain focused on their academic pursuits and not to allow their energies to be diverted by calls to protest,â Pathak said.The association also asked students to repose faith in the governmentâs efforts to strengthen the examination system rather than be influenced by ârumour and speculationâ.âThe Honâble Prime Minister has himself appealed to students and has assured the nation that all possible steps will be taken to ensure that future examinations are conducted in a completely fair, transparent and secure manner,â the letter said.Pathak asked university heads to personally engage with students, mentor them and keep campuses âcalm and focusedâ.âI am confident that, with your personal attention and compassionate leadership, our campuses will remain calm and focused, and our students will devote their full energies to their studies and to nation-building,â he said.

World.title: Centre appoints 1989-batch IAS officer Anurag Jain as NITI Aayog CEO
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday appointed Anurag Jain, a 1989-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the Madhya Pradesh cadre, as the new Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of

, the governmentâs apex public policy think tank.

The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has approved Jainâs appointment as CEO of NITI Aayog, effective from the date he assumes charge of the post, according to an official statement.

The statement said Jain will continue in the role for two years thereafter, or until further orders, whichever is earlier.

World.title: Centre unlikely to sack Pradhan over NEET row, open to compensate victims' kin: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre is unlikely to remove Union education minister

despite mounting demands for his resignation, as it believes he cannot be held responsible for the NEET paper leak, news agency PTI reported, citing a senior government functionary.

According to the report, the government is, however, willing to favourably consider the demand for compensation for the families of students who died by suicide following the alleged paper leak.

The Centre is also open to engaging seriously with protesters led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), though it believes there should be flexibility over the venue of the talks, instead of insisting on a particular location, the functionary told PTI.

The report added that the government has held a series of meetings on the issue involving Union home minister Amit Shah, health minister JP Nadda, commerce minister Piyush Goyal and Pradhan.

The development comes after Nadda, at a press conference on Wednesday, reiterated the Centre's willingness to discuss the alleged NEET paper leak in Parliament under any format and for any duration agreed upon by the Opposition.





"We have wanted this issue to be discussed in Parliament. Whether it is a short-duration discussion or a long-duration discussion, you decide how much time you want. The government is ready for discussion, and the Opposition should not keep changing the goalpost," he said.

Calling Parliament the appropriate forum to address the issue, Nadda urged both the government and the opposition to work together on a long-term solution.

"Children are ours, yours, and the future of the country. It is the responsibility of both the government and the Opposition to protect their future. We should discuss every aspect and come up with a concrete policy," he said.

Earlier in the day, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called for Pradhan's resignation, saying it was among the protesters' "non-negotiable" demands.

The CJP has been spearheading protests over the alleged examination irregularities since June.

Its Parliament march on July 20 saw students and supporters attempting to reach Parliament despite heavy police barricading, lathi-charge and the use of tear gas. The march was eventually halted near Parliament Street, where multiple layers of barricades had been erected.

World.title: Chipko movement was a challenge to hierarchy of development: Murali Sivaramakrishnan
World.content:
The Chipko movement was not merely a sustenance movement but also a challenge to the hierarchy of development, poet, painter, and academic Murali Sivaramakrishnan has said.

He was speaking on 50 years of Chipko, a seminal environment movement in India in the early 1970s, at a discussion on a book, 50 Years of Chipko – the Movement and its Afterlives, that has been edited by him, at an event organised by the Institute of English and the publishers Orient BlackSwan here on Wednesday.

Mr. Sivaramakrishnan pointed out that Chipko was an awakening. It eventually grew into talking about environment protection. It started in the Himalayas but spread quickly. It questioned how development was perceived to be urbanisation.

Mr. Sivaramakrishnan also spoke about the collaborators on the book and their perspectives such as ecofeminism, ecocinema, deep ecology, gender, and so on.

On the meaning of Chipko in the present, Mr. Sivaramakrishnan pointed out that recently, felling of trees for highway widening in Uttarakhand had been halted temporarily by the government following widespread public protests. “The book establishes a connection between human beings and nature. There has to be compassion for one another and for nature,” he concluded.

Jancy James, former Vice-Chancellor, who along with educator and entrepreneur Kalyani Vallath gave an overview of of 50 years of Chipko, said it was not merely an environmental movement but a philosophy of the relationship between humans and nature. The book, she said, was an eyeopener for those who thought about what nature meant and what humanity had been doing to nature.

Ms. Vallath said it was exciting to take a look through the book at the tradition of people’s voices. Chipko was not a single ideology promoted by one leader, but saw the involvement of so many people. The book treated the forest as ecosystem, historical archive, cultural text, sacred landscape, and political territory.

Referring to the landslips in Wayanad in recent times, Usha V.T., former head of the Centre for Women’s Studies, Pondicherry University, questioned why human beings could not see that to survive they need to preserve trees. She also spoke about how Chipko had affected the ecofeminist movement that existed even before the term ecofeminist came to be.

C.A. Lal, head of the Institute of English, delivered the welcome address.

The book contains 13 essays by 12 contributors and offers various perspectives of the movement’s impact in Indian environmental policies and global cultural narratives and thought.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Internet shut down, police use tear gas at Sansad Marg, as crowd of protesters swells
World.content:
The issue of NEET paper leak and police crackdown on protesters at Jantar Mantar and neighbouring areas rocked both Houses of Parliament on Wednesday (July 22, 2026). The government offered an elaborate discussion on the issue and accused the opposition of not allowing a debate by disrupting proceedings.

Meanwhile, large groups of people, including supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), continue to join the sit-in at Jantar Mantar on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), with the CJP saying “millions more will come” to Delhi if the government doesn’t agree to its demands, primarily the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET ‘paper’ leak issue.

Activist Sonam Wangchuk said he would end his indefinite hunger strike if the Centre gives an unequivocal assurance that no punitive or retaliatory action would be taken against students and youth who participated in the protest against alleged examination irregularities.

Also read: Police file four FIRs amid flak over crackdown on protesters

Delhi High Court on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) sought response of the Centre and the Delhi Police on petitions highlighting use of “excessive force” against protesters during the CJP-led march at Parliament on July 20. The Court also directed the Delhi Police to preserve all records relating to the incident, including CCTV footage and videography, if any, in accordance with the SOPs in place.

Also read: Hundreds of people order food online for protestors at Jantar Mantar

Follow for updates:

World.title: Sikkim tunnel disaster toll rises to 15; search continues for 10 trapped workers
World.content:
The death toll in the Sikkim tunnel disaster rose to 15 on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), as multiple agencies continued search and rescue operations for the remaining 10 workers inside.

According to National Hydroelectric Power Corporation Limited (NHPC), 25 were trapped after the sudden release of suspected methane gas caused an explosion inside the under-construction head race tunnel for its Teesta State-VI Hydroelectric Project at Samardung in Sikkim’s Namchi district. The accident occurred at 1.04 p.m. on July 20.

In a statement on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), the NHPC said rescue operations were continuing round the clock in close coordination with the Namchi district administration, the National Disaster Response Force, the State Disaster Response Force, Patel Engineering Limited, Eastern Coalfields Limited, Western Coalfields Limited, local authorities, and other agencies.

“Of the 25 personnel trapped inside the tunnel, 13 bodies have been retrieved so far. Every possible effort continues to be made to locate the remaining personnel,” said the statement issued in the afternoon. Later in the day, Namchi’s District Magistrate Anupa Tamling said two more bodies were retrieved from the tunnel. “The toll is 15 now,” she told The Hindu.

Announcing an ex gratia payment of ₹5 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, the NHPC also said its top officials were present at the site, closely monitoring and coordinating the rescue operations.

Slush hampers search

The Sikkim government said rainfall and the accumulation of large volumes of mud and water inside the tunnel had briefly hampered the search.

“Rescue teams continue to carry out intensive search and recovery operations under extremely challenging conditions, with sustained efforts focused on locating the remaining trapped persons,” a government spokesperson said.

On Tuesday (July 21, 2026), Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang briefed Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah about the ongoing rescue operations. Both assured Mr. Tamang of all possible assistance from the Centre.

World.title: NEET: Congress, BJP workers detained during rival protests in Bengaluru
World.content:
The Bengaluru police on Wednesday detained several Congress workers after they gathered outside the BJP’s State headquarters in Malleswaram and attempted to stage a protest in violation of restrictions imposed under High Court directions.

BJP leaders led by Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok staged a counter-protest in front of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) office on Queen’s Road. The police also detained Mr. Ashok and other BJP workers, stating that the demonstration violated the same High Court restrictions on public protests. They were taken to the High Grounds police Station and were later released.

Slogans against PM

At the Congress protest, the party workers held placards, raised slogans and allegedly attempted to lay siege to the BJP office. They were protesting against the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) irregularities, the police lathi-charge on protesters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, and the detention of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other Congress leaders. Youth Congress members burnt effigies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak.

The police intervened and took the demonstrators into preventive detention, citing High Court orders that permit public protests only at the designated protest venue, Freedom Park. Security was tightened in and around the BJP headquarters, with barricades erected to prevent any breach of law and order.

BJP alleges attack

After holding a protest in front of the KPCC office, Mr. Ashok submitted a petition to the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner alleging that Congress workers attacked BJP leaders. He claimed that eggs, iron rods and clubs were used in the assault and alleged that even the police bus carrying detained BJP workers to the police station was targeted. Miscreants threw eggs on BJP MLA B.P. Harish, the BJP said.

In his complaint, Mr. Ashok sought a detailed investigation into the incident and demanded strict action against those responsible. The situation remained under control following the preventive detentions, with heavy police deployment continuing in the area.

World.title: Crime Branch to re-arrest Dr. M.K Ram in Nithin Raj death case
World.content:
Crime Branch SP M. Mohanachandran on Wednesday said the investigating agency would re-arrest Dr. M.K. Ram, the first accused in the death of first-year BDS student Nithin Raj of Kannur Dental College, Anjarakandy. A fresh Crime Branch team has taken over the probe and commenced its investigation in Kannur.

Addressing the media, Mr. Mohanachandran said DySP Jeevan George has been entrusted with leading the investigation, and an application seeking permission to re-arrest Dr. Ram has already been filed before the court, and further action will be taken in accordance with the court’s order.

The Crime Branch will record the statements of Nithin Raj’s family members again to determine whether any aspect of the case were overlooked during the earlier investigation. The team will also examine the alleged involvement of loan app operators in connection with the student’s death.

The SP said the Crime Branch has already submitted its explanation before the court regarding the lapses pointed out in the earlier investigation. The fresh probe began on Wednesday after the new investigating team arrived in Kannur.

World.title: 19-year-old may lose vision in right eye due to pellet injury, says family
World.content:
A 19-year-old protester hit by a pellet gun during police action at the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP)July 20 march to Parliament may lose vision in his right eye, his family said.

Sahil Lochab, a resident of Najafgarh in southwest Delhi, underwent a surgery to remove pellets at the AIIMS Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Centre on Tuesday (July 21, 2026). Doctors have informed that there is only a “1% chance” of vision returning in the injured eye as the pupil was damaged, his family said.

Also Read: CJP protest Live updates on July 22, 2026

Mr. Lochab, who wants to join the police, is a student of Delhi University’s School of Open Learning. His mother, Jyoti, said, “He had attended the CJP protests before and went again on Monday (July 20), saying it was important and would help his studies... He always wanted to become a police officer. He is pursuing a distance-learning course while preparing for competitive examinations.”

Ms. Jyoti said that her son will undergo another surgery soon.

Parvesh, a childhood friend of Mr. Lochab, said, “Sahil said he was hit directly in his eye. From what we have been told, a second operation for his pupils will determine whether his vision will return to normal.” He added that Mr. Lochab is not yet able to see and is in a lot of pain.

Mr. Parvesh said his friend “was vocal about education issues” ever since he was a child and has been studying for the Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level examination.

Just like Mr. Mansoori, Mr. Lochab was taken to LHMC and then transferred to the AIIMS trauma centre.

Though Delhi Police had denied the use of pellet guns, Mr. Lochab’s family said it was told that the injuries were caused by pellets. A hospital source confirmed it.

On Wednesday, The Hindu reported that how pellet guns, technically known as pump action guns, were likely used against protesters on July 20. This was the first known instance of security forces using pellet guns on civilians in Delhi. One of the 80 injured protesters, identified as Shaikh Irshad Mansoori, underwent surgery at Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC) on Tuesday to remove a metal pellet lodged under his eye.

Mr. Mansoori will undergo another surgery and is likely to be transferred to another hospital with the necessary equipment. A hospital source said the pellets that have injured the two were of metal, not plastic.

Pellets guns and shock-batons are part of the gear of the Rapid Action Force (RAF), the specialised anti-riot unit under the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), which was deployed alongside Delhi Police on July 20 in and around Jantar Mantar. RAF, being a Central force, was deployed at the request of Delhi Police and remained under its operational control at the time of incident.

There has been no response from the CRPF on the use of pellet guns.

Meanwhile, Sakshi, 21, who sustained critical injuries during the protest, was removed from ventilator support after she responded to treatment, as per a statement by Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital on Wednesday. “She has been successfully extubated (removed from the ventilator) and is now breathing on her own. She is conscious and responding appropriately to commands. Her MRI of the brain and spine is normal,” it said.

World.title: Vismaya Mohanlal, other Malayalam actors face online harassment over support to Jantar Mantar protests
World.content:
Actor Vismaya Mohanlal, Mohanlal’s daughter, as well as other Malayalam film stars who extended support to the anti-government student agitation at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, have been facing vicious online harassment on social media platforms, especially Facebook.

Earlier this week, Vismaya had re-posted a story on her Instagram feed, condemning the Delhi Police’s actions to ‘suppress’ student protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over NEET paper leak and examination reforms.

“Tear gas. Lathi charges. Students injured. Roads blocked. Metro stations closed. Heavy barricading across the city. Internet suspension. You don’t have to agree with the protesters. You don’t have to support their demands. You don’t even have to like the organisations involved. But if the response to citizens raising their voices is overwhelming force instead of dialogue, every one of us should stop and ask what kind of democracy we are becoming. Because tomorrow, it could be you asking to be heard. Your city. Your neighbourhood. Your own family,” the post read.

The post ended with the line: “My question to all of you is simple: Do you genuinely believe this is how a democracy should respond to its own citizens.”

After the post went viral, some of the older posts on her Facebook page were flooded with hundreds of abusive comments. Some of the comments connected her comments at this juncture to the release of her upcoming debut film Thudakkam.

“You can ask your father about Prithviraj’s plight before making such comments,” read one of the comments, referring to the abusive attacks. Actor Prithviraj Sukumaran had faced flak after making public comments on political issues in the past.

Some of the other comments resorted to whataboutery, questioning her silence on various other issues, while others vowed never to watch her films. The abusive comments were lesser on her Instagram page compared to the Facebook page, a possible reflection of the different age profiles of the users of both platforms.

Actor Tovino Thomas, who is also at the receiving end of online harassment, had criticised the way the Delhi Police had handled the protests.

“When the future generation of a nation speaks up, and their voices are met with repressive force, it is the future itself that is being stamped down. It is faith in democracy that is being drained away. What did these students do wrong? Did they destroy property? Did they resort to violence? What exactly did they do to deserve this treatment? To every person protesting for a just cause, peacefully, in any part of our country, I extend my wholehearted solidarity. The right to dissent is not a threat to democracy; in fact it is one of its foundations,” he wrote.

He also rejected those who question his sense of nationalism. “I know myself better than you do. My politics is humanity. My belief is peace,” he wrote.

Some of the comments against Mr. Thomas were of a communal nature.

Actor Dulquer Salmaan said on Wednesday that “what’s happening at Jantar Mantar is a reminder to pause, listen and choose understanding” as he observed that “seeing young people face uncertainty is gut wrenching”.

In a social media post on the ongoing student protest, he said that education has always been about hope, opportunity, and the promise of a better future. “What breaks my heart even more is knowing some students feel they have no way forward, whilst others even choosing to end everything. And parents carrying that pain and debts trying to keep their hopes alive,” he said.

The actor pointed out that “beyond every opinion are individuals with dreams, aspirations, families, and hopes that deserve compassion and respect”. “My hope is for meaningful dialogue, peaceful resolutions, and decisions guided by wisdom and empathy. A future built on understanding will always be stronger than one built on division and violence,” he said

Last week, actor Parvathy Thiruvothu had also faced similar online harassment after she had made comments critical of the way educationist Sonam Wangchuk was shifted to a hospital from the protest site where he had been on an indefinite hunger strike. Ms. Thiruvothu called the act an “abduction of our rights”.

“Abduction of our voices. When the protectors become the abusers, we better remind them that we will never let OUR India be run by crooks and liars. Solidarity and support to the brave citizens at Jantar Mantar and across the country,” she wrote in an Instagram post.

Popular anchor Ranjini Haridas also faced severe online harassment after she visited Jantar Mantar to express solidarity with the students two days ago.

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader B. Gopalakrishnan was among those who made derogatory comments against her.

World.title: Centre steps up outreach to Wangchuk, agitators; activist puts a rider to call off protest
World.content:
The government on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) moved up a notch its engagement with protesters against the NEET paper leakage, with Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh meeting activist Sonam Wangchuk, who responded from hospital with a statement that he was willing to call off the hunger strike if the Centre gave an assurance that no punitive or retaliatory action would be taken against the protesting students.

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE updates - July 22, 2026

Mr. Wangchuk’s statement also stated that the Ministers assured him of “a meaningful discussion in Parliament to ensure accountability, including consideration of the resignation of the Education Minister.” The statement appeared to be a change from earlier, when the resignation of the Education Minister had been the top demand. Late on Tuesday evening, Mr. Nadda and Mr. Singh, after a marathon meeting with Home Minister Amit Shah, made their way to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram, where Mr. Wangchuk has now been moved for treatment, and, as per sources, urged Mr. Wangchuk to appeal to students to repose faith in the government’s process and avoid further escalation.

By evening, Mr. Wangchuk put out his statement, where he noted that he had been visited by around 65 members of Parliament from various political parties who had also urged him to end his strike. He therefore requested “an unequivocal assurance from the government that none of the young protesters will face any punitive or retaliatory legal action for participating in this movement. Their only ‘offence’ has been to raise their voice for a fair and accountable education system.”

Coordination with States

Sources in the government said they were also going to coordinate with State governments on working out compensation for families that lost their children because of death by suicide attributed to cancellation of NEET exams.

Addressing a press conference on Wednesday evening, Mr. Nadda, the main interlocutor for the government, said he was in talks with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), and had met the delegation from that organisation, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, in a “good atmosphere” and had asked them to put their demands in writing. “We are in talks and we will continue to engage,” he said but admitted that no meeting with CJP leaders had taken place on Wednesday. He reiterated that Parliament was the correct forum to discuss the issue threadbare and that it required the government and the Opposition to come up with long lasting solutions for the paper leakage issue.

The government, therefore, appears to be more proactive in its outreach to quell the storm of protests on the NEET issue, which, some in the government admitted had taken them by surprise on July 20 with a well-attended protest march with an organically mobilised student protesters.

According to one senior Minister in the Union government in the know of things, the outreach to the CJP representatives and to Mr. Wangchuk was only one part of what the government and the BJP now feel is an issue they will have to deal with in a more seminal manner. “The protests are one part of the issue, even the Congress protesting is a more familiar ground of political combat for the party, but the number of people especially youngsters who are aggrieved, not just with regard to NEET but also anxieties regarding their future is something that we have to deal with,” he said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi had, during one of his public meetings, countered the Congress’s “jitni abaadi utna haq” (to each according to their number) formulation for social justice based on a caste census, by coming up with four categories, which, he said, were universally applicable across India, farmers, poor, women and the youth. The NEET paper leakage protests have seriously dented the BJP’s appeal in the youth section of that formulation, a political conundrum the party knows it has to deal with before the Uttar Pradesh polls early next year.

World.title: ‘Would expect India to be concerned’: Rubio on Trump’s generic drug tariffs
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday addressed the proposed tariffs on generic drugs being brought into America and said India did not raise any concern over President Donald Trump’s tariff announcement during their meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.

During a meeting in Manila on Wednesday, Jaishankar met Rubio to discuss priority areas, including trade, tariffs, energy, defence, critical minerals, and artificial intelligence.

JUST IN: 🇺🇸🇮🇳 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said India did not raise concerns over President Trump’s proposed tariffs on generic drugs during their meeting. Rubio added that the United States remains “very close” to India and understands New Delhi’s concerns over the issue. pic.twitter.com/J9gI8jgWN3 — Asia Nexus (@nexusasian) July 22, 2026

Rubio: India did not raise drug tariff issue

Rubio, while taking questions from reporters, was asked if he had any discussion regarding the generic drugs tariff proposed by the Trump administration and if Jaishankar raised any concern about the tariffs announced.

Always good to see my friend, Indian External Affairs Minister @DrSJaishankar on the sidelines of ASEAN. We discussed regional security issues, the Quad, trade, and defense agreements. Our relationship with India is vitally important. pic.twitter.com/Ji7umqLO7K — Secretary Marco Rubio (@SecRubio) July 22, 2026

Rubio responded, saying that “We didn’t get into depth on pharmaceuticals today, but I would expect them to be concerned about it, but they didn’t raise it today.”

Pleased to meet @SecRubio of the USA here in Manila. Our meeting focused on areas which are priority for the 🇮🇳🇺🇸 Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership, including trade & tariffs, energy, defence & security, critical minerals & artificial intelligence. We also exchanged… pic.twitter.com/dCc9YpQAEp — Dr. S. Jaishankar (@DrSJaishankar) July 22, 2026

The US Secretary of State added that India “might have raised concerns with others in our system because we were obviously deal with India; we are very close to them.”



West Asia crisis also figures in discussions

According to a PTI report, Jaishankar and Rubio also exchanged views on the West Asia crisis and its larger impact on global fuel supplies and market stability.

Jaishankar highlights strategic partnership agenda

Informing about the discussion, Jaishankar in a social media post wrote, “Our meeting focused on areas which are priority for the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership, including trade and tariffs, energy, defence and security, critical minerals and artificial intelligence.”

The external affairs minister added, “We also exchanged quick perspectives on regional, global and multilateral issues of mutual interest.”

Jaishankar and Rubio are in the Philippines to participate in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the Quad grouping and take part in the high-level discussions under the framework.

Trump announces phased tariff plan for generic drugs

The development comes as Trump on Tuesday said all generic drugs being brought into America will continue to have a tariff of 0 per cent for two years starting from August 1, and after that the tariff rate will be hiked to 100 per cent for one year and to 200 per cent thereafter.



In a post on Truth Social, the US President wrote, “This is done in order to RESHORE ⁠Generic Pharmaceutical Production into America, with a penalty ​to those Companies that decide not to build ​Plant and Equipment within the stated period of time given to them.”

World.title: Salman Khan supports CJP protest: ‘Heart goes out to students who were hurt’
World.content:
Actor Salman Khan has extended his support to the Cockroach Janta Party-led student protest over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak. The star — perhaps the biggest celebrity to comment on the issue — said he was glad that the students had come together to demand a better educational system, adding that the government should listen to their demands.

Taking to social media late on Wednesday, Salman wrote, “It was such a peaceful movement, feel so sad that it had to take a violent turn. My heart goes out to the students and their families who were hurt. Paper leak is a very serious issue, and I am glad to know n see that the kids of our country have come together for a better educational system, and their parents supported them.”

World.title: 200 detained, released after several gather to support Sonam Wangchuk
World.content:
Hundreds of young men and women took part in a demonstration held in solidarity with activist Sonam Wangchuk and Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, here on Wednesday.

The roads outside the Gujarat University, where the protest was held, swarmed with policemen, police vans and patrolling vehicles since the afternoon. While it was not clear who announced it, the demonstration was scheduled around 6 pm.



Even as the number of protesters who walked the several lanes and bylanes around the university to join the call swelled, police prevented people from congregating and detained those who held placards and shouted slogans.

Among those detained was Jignya Vyas, a popular Gujarati theatre actor who got into a police van reciting the famous lines by Shailendra—”Tu zinda hai toh zindagi ki jeet pe yakeen kar”.

World.title: Ayush Shetty beats Alwi Farhan in battle of future stars
World.content:
Ayush Shetty secured a remarkably comfortable 21-17, 5-21, 21-17 victory over Indonesian rival Alwi Farhan to enter the second round of the Super 1000 China Open. It was an important win on a big stage — a Super 1000 — against an opponent who is the season’s best form player and widely acknowledged as Indonesia’s next big hope.

The two 21-year-olds are seen as the future of badminton, though they have done enough to be considered the present. While Alwi has two titles this season, Ayush is still searching for his big one. China Open offers a good opportunity for the World No.23. Though his draw half is stacked — including Lakshya Sen in the semis possibly — he can dream big, after securing a confidence-boosting result, getting past a 2022 World Jrs batchmate who he hadn’t beaten since 2023.

Ayush plays Nhat Nguyen, a pokey tricky Irishman next.

Sen registered a fighting win over Yushi Tanaka after an especially tricky first set, where he contrived to make a 17-14 lead needlessly adventurous. He won 22-20, 15-21, 21-14 highlighting yet another slow start to a tournament, and Round 2 looks ominous.



They are only 1-1 in head to head, but Sen and Candian Victor Lai have a propensity to play memorable matches, so Thursday would be no different. Had badminton been at the Commonwealth Games, Lai would’ve fought Sen hard for the gold. Just as Lai, who won the last Super 1000 at Indonesia entered Top 10, Sen has fallen back to World No.14. It is pretty clear Sen will prioritise the big events. But he would be keen to join Saina Nehwal, Kidambi Srikanth and PV Sindhu as the only Indians in singles to win China Open. The relentless retriever and snappy attacker Lai won’t make it easy, though Sen has a more rounded game than him.

While the All England semifinals was one of the classics, and a match Sen will take plenty of hope from, the Thomas Cup loss would’ve stung him. Sen was 21-18, 19-19 rallying from 16-19 down when he couldn’t forge ahead. Lai is very beatable with Sen’s skillset, but the Indian has allowed him to get into his head with his expansive smashes.



The draw is treacherous for Sen with Loh Kean or Jojo Christie after Lai.

Sindhu advances

Sindhu’s attack has looked terrifying for her opponents. (BWF/Badminton Photo) Sindhu’s attack has looked terrifying for her opponents. (BWF/Badminton Photo)

In women’s singles, Japan Open winner PV Sindhu started out avenging an upstart loss to Unnati Hooda, who had famously beaten her at China last season.

The 21-14, 9-21, 21-10 win for Sindhu saw two fairly one-sided sets with a breather set lost in between. Sindhu however immediately runs into Chinese Chen Yufei who had retired with hamstring issues after finding herself at the end of a Sindhu torrent last week.

The Chinese remains iffy in her court movements and the Indian will sniff a chance should Yufei continue being tentative. Playing at home presents a different pressure for the Chinese, though she might have rested more, given she wrapped up by Saturday, and was airdropped in place of An Se-young who herself withdrew from China.



Sindhu’s attack has looked terrifying for her opponents, with Yufei telling BWF, “I wanted to play at 100%, but Sindhu played very well. Her attack was explosive and I was always defending. I wasn’t comfortable.” Acupuncture and massage had both not offered her relief last week, but playing in front of her home crowd, Yufei will pose a stronger resolve to Sindhu.

World.title: Priyanka Chopra says motherhood changed career priorities: ‘Don’t just pack bags and go…’
World.content:
For years, Priyanka Chopra’s career was defined by an extraordinarily demanding schedule. At the peak of her Bollywood career, she starred in multiple films each year, constantly travelling between shoots, promotions and international commitments. But since becoming a mother to daughter Malti Marie, the actor says her relationship with work has undergone a significant shift.

Speaking at the Cannes Lions 2026 conference in France, Priyanka reflected on how motherhood has reshaped her priorities. “Your priorities really change. I don’t just pack my bags and go off for a movie anymore,” she said. She added, “I don’t do five films a year. I don’t travel the way I used to. I’m really, really selective about the time I spend and who I spend it with.” Opening up about this new phase of life, Priyanka also admitted, “I’m navigating working-mom life. I have so much more respect for my mother now.”

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

This is a perspective she has spoken about before. In an interview for Marie Claire’s March 2026 issue, Priyanka shared that while she once wanted to “juggle all the balls and do all the things,” she now trusts her instincts more and feels more comfortable saying no to projects that do not fit her priorities. She also revealed that she experiences anxiety when her four-year-old daughter, Malti, is away from her, even during school hours.

But how does parenthood often change the way people think about ambition, work-life balance and success?



How parenthood reshapes work priorities

Sonal Khangarot, licensed rehabilitation counsellor and psychotherapist, The Answer Room, tells indianexpress.com, “For many parents, particularly mothers, the arrival of a child often leads to a profound shift in identity and priorities. Becoming a parent can activate a stronger need for emotional connection, caregiving, and a sense of responsibility, which naturally influences how one views work and success. Many women begin to reassess what fulfilment means to them, moving from external achievements to seeking a better balance between professional aspirations and family life.”

There is also an increased awareness of time, Khangarot adds, with many wanting to be more present during their child’s formative years. Additionally, societal expectations and the mental load of caregiving can contribute to this change in priorities. It’s important to remember that this transition isn’t about becoming less ambitious; rather, it’s about redefining ambition in a way that aligns with one’s evolving values, emotional needs, and sense of purpose.



Balancing career ambitions with family responsibilities

For many parents, particularly mothers, the arrival of a child often leads to a profound shift in identity and priorities. Becoming a parent can activate a stronger need for emotional connection, caregiving, and a sense of responsibility, which naturally influences how one views work and success.

Khangarot states that many women begin to reassess what fulfilment means to them, moving from external achievements to seeking a better balance between professional aspirations and family life. There is also an increased awareness of time, with many wanting to be more present during their child’s formative years. “Additionally, societal expectations and the mental load of caregiving can contribute to this change in priorities. It’s important to remember that this transition isn’t about becoming less ambitious; rather, it’s about redefining ambition in a way that aligns with one’s evolving values, emotional needs, and sense of purpose.”



Setting boundaries and redefining success

As we move through different life stages, our definition of success naturally evolves. Khangarot mentions, “Early in our careers, success may mean saying yes to every opportunity, but over time many people realise that constantly being available can lead to burnout and resentment.”

What does success mean to you right now? Click on the statement that best reflects your current mindset: ‘I say yes to every opportunity because I don’t want to miss out.’ Early in a career, saying yes can create valuable opportunities. Over time, however, constantly being available may lead to burnout if it comes at the expense of your wellbeing. ‘I’m learning to say no so I can focus on what matters most.’ Setting boundaries is not selfish. Protecting your time and energy allows you to invest more fully in the people, goals and responsibilities that align with your values.
