World.title: China-Proposed Global AI Organization Launched at WAIC
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018788/China-Proposed Global AI Organization Launched at WAIC
World.content:
SHANGHAI – China’s World AI Conference (WAIC) kicked off on Friday in Shanghai, one day after 29 countries agreed to establish a global organization dedicated to collaborating on AI innovation, development, and governance.

Termed the “World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization,” or WAICO, China first proposed the initiative at last year’s WAIC. Signatories include Kazakhstan, Laos, Pakistan, Russia, and Indonesia.

The annual conference, held this year from July 17 to 20, was founded in 2018 by multiple national ministries and the Shanghai municipal government to connect AI companies, researchers, and developers.

This year’s event featured a keynote speech by Chinese President Xi Jinping, as well as over 1,100 international AI companies showcasing more than 3,000 cutting-edge products and technologies, including over 300 global debuts, such as an agentic AI smartphone, which can operate autonomously rather than simply responding to users’ commands.

The event also welcomed other world leaders, including United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.

In his keynote speech at the conference’s opening, Xi said that AI is emerging as a new engine of economic growth and is moving from the “digital world” into the “physical world.”

“We should seize this opportunity to promote open collaboration, accelerate innovation, and expand real-world applications so that AI can empower industries across the economy,” Xi said.

He also called for enhanced alignment and coordination to develop a consensus-based global AI governance framework that better benefits humanity.

Wang Tianchan, an AI research fellow at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies (SIIS), told Sixth Tone that Xi’s attendance reflects that the event aligns with the country’s broader national priorities.

Xi also announced that China will invite 5,000 individuals from developing countries to partake in AI training opportunities over the next five years. China will also establish international AI application cooperation centers with regional organizations, including the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, the Arab League, the African Union, and the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States.

The AI race has moved beyond models and chatbots, Gu Jiawei, founder and CEO of AI startup Ling.ai, told Sixth Tone.

“The next breakthrough will happen in the real world — whether AI can understand its environment, proceed through successive situations, and work reliably under complex constraints,” he said. “What matters most at WAIC is seeing intelligence move from demonstration into daily life.”

With AI becoming a strategic technology shaping economic growth and global competition, WAIC has also expanded beyond technology showcases to include discussions on AI governance, international cooperation, and the industry’s future. Beginning in 2024, the conference has been held alongside the country’s “High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance,” a platform for global AI dialogue.

“As AI reshapes the global landscape, the way we approach these conversations matters,” Wang, the SIIS research fellow, said. “An open, cooperative, and pragmatic approach is essential to answering one of the most critical questions today: where should AI go next?”



Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: A visitor interacts with an AI-powered companion robot at the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai, July 17, 2026. VCG)

World.title: Low pressure area develops into Tropical Depression Kiyapo
World.content:
KIYAPO. Satellite image of Tropical Depression Kiyapo as of July 22, 2026, 10 pm.

Tropical Depression Kiyapo is the Philippines' 11th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the fourth for July alone

MANILA, Philippines – The low pressure area inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) developed into a tropical depression at 8 pm on Wednesday, July 22.

It was given the local name Kiyapo, as the country’s 11th tropical cyclone for 2026. It is also the fourth tropical cyclone for July alone.

As of 10 pm on Wednesday, Kiyapo was located 1,080 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon, moving northwest at 25 kilometers per hour (km/h).

The tropical depression has maximum sustained winds of 45 km/h and gustiness of up to 55 km/h.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said Kiyapo could go near or make landfall in Cagayan province’s Babuyan Islands by Friday evening, July 24. Landfall in mainland Cagayan is not being ruled out as well.

While approaching Cagayan, Kiyapo might intensify into a tropical storm by Friday. It may even reach severe tropical storm status ahead of its potential landfall.

In PAGASA’s initial Kiyapo bulletin issued at 11 pm on Wednesday, it already raised Signal No. 1 for portions of Cagayan and Isabela, giving them lead time of 36 hours to prepare for strong winds:

eastern part of mainland Cagayan (Santa Ana, Gonzaga, Lal-lo, Gattaran, Baggao, Peñablanca, Santa Teresita, Buguey)

eastern part of Isabela (Maconacon, San Pablo, Cabagan, Tumauini, Ilagan City, Divilacan, Palanan, San Mariano, Dinapigue)

The highest possible tropical cyclone wind signal due to Kiyapo could be Signal No. 2 or 3.

PAGASA added that the southwest monsoon or habagat and the periphery or outer bands of the tropical cyclone will bring strong to gale-force gusts to the following areas:

Thursday, July 23

most of Mindanao, Siquijor, Bohol, Southern Leyte

Friday, July 24

most of the country

The weather bureau also warned Northern Luzon to brace for moderate to intense rain from Kiyapo in the coming days. Here is the latest rainfall outlook for the tropical cyclone, released at 11 pm on Wednesday:

Thursday evening, July 23, to Friday evening, July 24

Heavy to intense rain (100-200 millimeters): Cagayan

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Batanes, Isabela, Apayao, Kalinga, Abra, Ilocos Norte

Friday evening, July 24, to Saturday evening, July 25

Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Cagayan, Apayao, Abra, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Batanes, Isabela, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Benguet, La Union

Aside from Kiyapo, the southwest monsoon will be bringing moderate to heavy rain, too.

Wednesday evening, July 22, to Thursday evening, July 23

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Zamboanga del Norte, Zamboanga Sibugay, Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Sultan Kudarat, Sarangani

Thursday evening, July 23, to Friday evening, July 24

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Antique, Negros Occidental, Negros Oriental, Zamboanga Sibugay, Zamboanga del Sur, Lanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte

Friday evening, July 24, to Saturday evening, July 25

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Occidental Mindoro, Antique, Iloilo, Guimaras, Negros Occidental

All areas to be affected by Kiyapo and the southwest monsoon should watch out for floods and landslides.

Moreover, in the next 24 hours, conditions in a few seaboards will be risky for small vessels.

Up to rough seas (small vessels should not venture out to sea)

Southeastern seaboard of Davao Oriental – waves up to 3 meters high

Up to moderate to rough seas (small vessels should take precautionary measures or avoid sailing, if possible)

Southern and remaining eastern seaboards of Davao Oriental – waves up to 2.5 meters high

Seaboards of Davao Occidental and Surigao del Sur – waves up to 2 meters high

After its potential landfall in Cagayan, Kiyapo could emerge over the Luzon Strait and eventually leave PAR by Saturday morning or noon, July 25. – Rappler.com

World.title: Too much speaking time? Senator Raffy Tulfo hits the buzzer.
World.content:
TULFO. Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo poses a question to National Bureau of Investigation BARMM Regional Director Attorney Jeremy Lotoc during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 14, 2026.

The Senate impeachment court's tiny buzzer and bell-ringer Anika steal the show on Day 9 of Vice President Sara Duterte's trial

The impeachment court’s tiny buzzer stole the spotlight on Wednesday, July 22.

Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo openly questioned why some senator-judges seemed to be getting extra time while others are cut off almost immediately.

Play Video

“Bakit kapag sa kabila pinapayagan sila 5 to 10 minutes. Bakit kapag sa amin, sa majority, kinu-cut agad nila ’yung time pagdating ng two minutes,” Tulfo asked. Nakakahalata na kami.”

(Why is it that the other side is allowed to speak for five to 10 minutes, but when it’s our turn, the majority, they cut us off the moment we reach the two-minute mark? We’ve noticed it.)

Tulfo said he nudges the Senate secretariat to hit the buzzer when colleagues go overtime.

“Kung minsan binubulungan ko na ’yung ano diyan, ’Uy, pindutin mo na ’yung bell para makapagsalita ‘yung iba,'” Tulfo said. (Sometimes I even whisper to the staff there, ‘Hey, ring the bell so the others can have a chance to speak.)

Inside the courtroom, Presiding Officer Chiz Escudero claimed that “there’s no majority nor minority. We are all senator-judges.”

During the trial, Escudero also made a shoutout to the mystery bell-ringer: Anika, a lawyer from the Senate secretariat. The courtroom erupted in laughter as the previously anonymous staff member was suddenly named in open court.

BELL RINGER. Anika, a lawyer from the Senate secretariat, serves as the bell ringer in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, on July 22, 2026.

Afterwards, the bell seemed to ring a little more cautiously.

Senators are typically given two minutes each. The timer is paused whenever a senator is not speaking. There are also digital clocks in the session hall synchronized with the secretariat’s timer.

However, some senator-judges still stretched their time, including senators Pia Cayetano and Imee Marcos.

At the back row, while Marcos was questioning the witness, the eyes of male senator-judges were on the buzzer.

Play Video

Senator Erwin Tulfo was seen taking the buzzer from Anika and placing it on their table.

Seated with him were Raffy Tulfo and Kiko Pangilinan, while Ping Lacson and Lito Lapid joined in as they joked, pointed at one another, and teased about who should press it.

Pangilinan eventually stood up and returned the buzzer to the Senate secretariat. He placed it on the ledge of the staff’s table.

But Raffy Tulfo’s intrusive thoughts seemed to kick in. He turned around and pressed the bell behind him.

The buzzer rang, but Senator Marcos kept speaking anyway.

The trial adjourned at 4:41 pm. Nine trial days down. Roughly 83 days more remain if the current estimate of 92 trial days holds.

Some hope to finish the trial before Christmas. Maybe, Anika, the bell ringer, or the presiding officer, might help speed things up. – Rappler.com

World.title: Defense asks Matibag: Didn’t you take Sara Duterte’s ‘threats’ out of context?
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines – The counsels of Vice President Sara Duterte continued to defend the Vice President in her impeachment case by casting doubt on the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI)’s assessment of her alleged threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

During the trial’s ninth day, defense lawyer Mark Vinluan played a portion of the October 2024 video of the Vice President where she said that she imagined herself cutting Marcos’ head. NBI Director Melvin Matibag confirmed that this was the source of the “cutting head” remarks that his bureau was looking into.

“Didn’t VP Sara say her statement in jest?” Vinluan asked.

Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro objected to the question, saying it was speculative. But presiding officer Senator Chiz Escudero ruled that Matibag may answer.

“Again, I cannot go into the state of mind of the Vice President, and precisely the reason why do’n sa pattern of violence, kasama po talaga ‘yan e…. ‘Pag pinagsama-sama po ‘yong amin pong imbestigasyon, ‘yong amin pong napanood, kasama po ‘yan, do’n po namin na-establish ‘yong isa do’n sa limang factors na pattern of violence,” Matibag responded.

(Again, I cannot go into the state of mind of the Vice President, and precisely the reason why that’s part of the pattern of violence. If we piece together our evidence, what we’ve watched, that’s part of…one of the five factors of the pattern of violence.)

Play Video

Vinluan then asked the NBI director if they had taken the Vice President’s statements out of context.

“Mahirap po para sa’ming law enforcement na ‘yong ganyang mga statement ay amin pong babalewalain…. Sa amin po sa law enforcement, we have to give credence to that and i-process po namin,” said Matibag.

(It’s hard for us law enforcement to neglect those statements…. For us law enforcement, we have to give credence to that and process it.)

The impeachment court held the last trial day for the grave threats allegations against the Vice President – the fourth article of impeachment – on Wednesday, July 22. The article includes Duterte’s November 2024 press conference where she announced that she had allegedly contracted a hitman to harm Marcos and his family if she gets killed. (READ: Sara Duterte: If I get killed, so will Marcos, Liza Araneta, Romualdez)

The prosecution and the NBI also looked into former incidents involving the Vice President in establishing her supposed history of violence. Apart from the past press conferences, the authorities also highlighted Duterte’s punching of sheriff Abe Andres in Davao City when she was mayor.

Andres was supposed to testify for the prosecution, but he was dropped as a witness alongside seven others.

Vinluan, during cross-examination, touched on this issue and indirectly explained the context behind the incident. He said, while interrogating Matibag, that Duterte punched Andres due to his refusal to give a two-hour extension to informal settlers during a demolition in 2011.

“So, in other words, are you also aware that it was the sheriff’s refusal to provide the two-hour extension? That’s why VP Sara got angry?” the defense counsel asked.

“Well, that is the claim of the then-mayor,” Matibag said in response.

Doubting Lascañas

The defense continued to cast doubt on the affidavit of self-confessed Davao Death Squad (DDS) member Arturo Lascañas during the continuance of Vinluan’s cross-examination. The defense even called the affidavit a mere scrap of paper.

Lascañas’ affidavit has been submitted to the International Criminal Court as part of the crimes against humanity case against the Vice President’s father, former president Rodrigo Duterte. The self-confessed DDS named the Vice President in his affidavit, claiming there that they had allegedly received kill orders from the former president, then later, from Sara as Davao City mayor.

As a blow to Lascañas, Vinluan raised his alleged perjury.

Vinluan asked Matibag if Lascañas was the same man who was recommended to be charged with perjury by the Senate panel led by Senator Ping Lacson. Matibag said he didn’t “hear” that Lascañas was charged with the said offense.

Later in the trial, Lacson interjected and clarified that Lascañas retracted and changed his testimony before the Senate, but the senator did not file a perjury complaint against him.

“Because of this committee report, I recommend amending the Revised Penal Code, particularly for the crime of perjury. But I just want to correct that I did not file a perjury [complaint],” Lacson said in his manifestation.

Vinluan later asked Matibag if the NBI immediately believed Lascañas’ claims. Matibag explained that they relied on his statements to establish Duterte’s alleged pattern of violence. – Rappler.com

World.title: BSP senior official hits bank secrecy limits in Sara Duterte subpoenas
World.content:
SEALED. The box containing Vice President Sara Duterte's tax records is presented before the House justice committee on April 29, 2026.

'The other day, the impeachment court issued an order to open bank deposits. But lo and behold, you cannot open FCDU deposits,' says BSP Deputy Governor Elmore Capule as he lamented the Philippines' outdated bank secrecy rules

MANILA, Philippines – A senior Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) official has criticized the country’s decades-old bank secrecy laws after the House prosecution’s attempt to examine Vice President Sara Duterte’s money trail was stopped at foreign currency deposits, which seem to remain beyond reach even in impeachment cases.

Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) Deputy Governor Elmore Capule referenced the Senate impeachment court’s decision as he sharply criticized bank secrecy laws that he said have frustrated investigators for decades.

“The other day, the impeachment court issued an order to open bank deposits. But lo and behold, you cannot open FCDU deposits,” Capule said during the signing of an information-sharing agreement between the BSP and the Department of Justice.

FCDU refers to foreign currency deposit unit accounts, which are commonly denominated in US dollars and other foreign currencies.

“We are talking of bank secrecy being used to hide illegal activities,” Capule added during his speech on Wednesday, July 22.

The Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, approved subpoenas on Monday, July 20, for bank and Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records involving Duterte, her husband Manases Carpio, and several linked companies.

The prosecution sought the records to establish a financial baseline that could be compared with the couple’s declared income, assets, liabilities, and business interests. The request forms part of the impeachment article accusing Duterte of amassing unexplained wealth.

But the court excluded the couple’s dollar accounts from the subpoenas because foreign currency deposits enjoy stricter protection under the Foreign Currency Deposit Act than peso accounts do under the Bank Secrecy Law. The Bank Secrecy Law expressly allows bank inquiries in impeachment cases. The Foreign Currency Deposit Act does not contain the same exception and requires the depositor’s written permission before an account may be examined.

That could leave prosecutors with only part of the possible financial picture, even after securing the impeachment court’s approval.

‘It can be used by criminals’

Capule is one of the BSP’s most senior legal officials. Before becoming deputy governor, he served as the central bank’s general counsel and spent years working on banking legislation and financial sector reforms. He was also closely involved in developing the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA), which created new powers for tracing money used in scams and money-muling.

His frustration and distaste with bank secrecy stems from one of his earliest brushes with possible government corruption. Capule recalled that one of the first cases he handled in government involved a state-owned corporation that transferred funds to a private account at the height of the EDSA revolution.

He said he argued that authorities should be allowed to examine the account because the deposited money was itself the subject of litigation.

It took about a year to secure a favorable ruling.

“Lo and behold, the fund was transferred one year before,” Capule said. “So what do we do now? We have to trace it. So essentially, it’s dead.”

“That is my first experience with the secrecy. It can be used by criminals. Thirty-five years later, fast forward, bank secrecy is still very much alive,” he added.

Capule also criticized the treatment of bank secrecy as it “mutated” into state policy under the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

“Whenever other jurisdictions see that, they are telling me, ‘Are you joking? Bank secrecy and then money laundering in one statute?’” he said.

Note that Capule did not allege that Duterte held undisclosed foreign currency deposits or that any account contained illegal proceeds. His biggest criticism is that the Philippines’ outdated bank secrecy laws can stop authorities from getting a complete financial trail.

AFASA, the new law that he helped craft, provides a narrow exception. In investigations involving financial scams and money-muling, a designated BSP officer may inquire into accounts, including foreign currency deposits, to trace disputed funds and help build cases.

Capule noted that this gives the BSP officer authority to examine foreign currency accounts “which the impeachment court cannot do.” That power, however, applies only to suspected violations of AFASA.

BSP has no role in subpoenas

BSP General Counsel Roberto Figueroa separately clarified that the central bank was not a recipient of the subpoenas and would not direct banks on how to respond.

“So far, we haven’t received any subpoena,” Figueroa told Rappler along the sidelines of the event.

The subpoenas were directed at individual banks, leaving their respective legal teams to determine how to respond, including whether to comply, raise objections, or seek clarification from the impeachment court.

“It’s for their own legal counsel to determine what they’re going to do, whether they’re going to comply with the subpoena or not,” Figueroa said.

He also stressed that the Anti-Money Laundering Council, which was separately ordered to submit financial records, is institutionally distinct from the BSP.

“I know the AMLC was mentioned,” he said. “But again, that’s AMLC, so that’s not BSP.”

Although BSP Governor Eli Remolona Jr. also chairs the AMLC, the council is a separate government agency with its own statutory powers, procedures, and confidentiality requirements. – Rappler.com

World.title: [In the Public Square] SONA: The view from outside Manila
World.content:
LIVE

A year ago, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. stood before a joint session of Congress and called out those involved in flood control corruption, saying, “Mahiya naman kayo (Have some shame)!”

In a long State of the Nation Address, that was what stood out. And this is what many who watch or read or listen to the SONA this year will expect: Real progress in the campaign against flood control corruption. Is there any?

We want to take a broader view of Marcos’ fifth SONA and our expectations by, well, going outside so-called Imperial Manila.

In this episode of In the Public Square, Rappler columnist John Nery is joined by lawyer Angelisa Razo, a professor of law at Ateneo de Davao University; Francis Allan Angelo, a newspaper editor-in-chief in Iloilo; and Jonas Cabiles Soltes, a public official in Camarines Sur.

World.title: Sara Duterte trial: Prosecution wraps up grave threats case
World.content:
3RD WITNESS. National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag testifies in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026.

The prosecution moves on to the presentation of its case on Duterte's alleged misuse of confidential funds when the trial resumes on July 29

MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution panel in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte finished on Wednesday, July 22, the presentation of the fourth impeachment article, which seeks to hold her liable for her threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

The prosecution waived its right to conduct a redirect examination of its third witness, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag, saying it was “unnecessary.”

Play Video

“If a conviction or acquittal is dependent alone on the evidence of the prosecution, then I can say very confidently that the prosecution has proven its case,” private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said in a press conference after the trial.

“But let us wait to hear what is the defense of the defense,” Kapunan added.

Play Video

The ninth day of the trial saw Duterte-allied senators try to assail the credibility of Matibag, with Senator Pia Cayetano even bringing up his supposed inconsistent statements about the Senate gunfight in May.

Aside from Matibag, the prosecution had presented two other witnesses — NBI senior agent John Mark Calilung, and former NBI cybercrime division chief and now BARMM Regional Director Jeremy Lotoc.

Their testimonies separately sought to prove that the video of Duterte’s virtual press conference where she uttered the threat was authentic, and that the statements were a serious and true grave threat, regardless of whether there was a condition or not.

The defense previously argued that Duterte’s conditional threat — to have the President killed if something bad were to happen to her — was justified.

The prosecution has insisted Duterte’s confession that she had hired an assassin was an “admission against interest.”

The NBI, however, has yet to locate the supposed hitman nearly two years since the threat was uttered.

Matibag told the court on Wednesday that the NBI had narrowed down the number of persons of interest to less than 20, but it would take the agency another three to six months to identify the assassin.

Play Video

Matibag said Duterte’s remark is no longer just a “threat” but a “plan” to kill the President, when taken up with other statements of the Vice President, as well as those of her brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte alluding to a Marcos decapitation scenario.

Matibag added that the NBI is investigating whether there is conspiracy between the siblings.

The prosecution also presented before the court videos of Mayor Sebastian’s remarks, as well as the affidavit of self-confessed Davao Death Squad hitman Arturo Lascañas, who had implicated the Vice President in the extrajudicial killings in Davao City when she was mayor.

Cayetano castigated the prosecution for presenting the affidavit despite the lack of notarization, but Luistro defended the move on Wednesday.

“It was never claimed by the prosecution that this affidavit is notarized,” Luistro said. “This was presented as part of the testimony of the witness and the NBI probe.”

When the trial resumes on Wednesday, July 29, the prosecution will move to the presentation of the article 1 of the impeachment complaint related to Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds. – Rappler.com

World.title: Clark Water boosts water security through proactive El Niño Mitigation Plan
World.content:
Manila Water Non-East Zone operating unit Clark Water continues to strengthen its water supply system through the implementation of a comprehensive El Niño Mitigation Plan, reinforcing its commitment to water security and reliable service delivery for customers across its service areas in Pampanga amid the challenges posed by prolonged dry weather. —Photo from Manila Water

MANILA, Philippines — Manila Water Non-East Zone operating unit Clark Water continues to strengthen its water supply system through the implementation of a comprehensive El Niño Mitigation Plan, reinforcing its commitment to water security and reliable service delivery for customers across the Clark Freeport Zone amid the challenges posed by prolonged dry weather conditions.

As climate variability and drought events increasingly impact water resource management, Clark Water has adopted a multi-faceted strategy focused on source sustainability, infrastructure development, operational readiness, and system resilience to ensure the continuous availability of water supply.

The El Niño Mitigation Plan fortifies Clark Water’s ability to manage limited water resources, optimize supply distribution, and maintain stable service levels during extended dry periods.

Article continues after this 

READ: Manila Water facilities among first under 100-kW RAP threshold

As part of its water supply augmentation initiatives, Clark Water is currently rehabilitating ten (10) existing wells to optimize production capacity. The company is also undertaking the redrilling of two (2) old and abandoned deep wells, while simultaneously developing two (2) new production wells to diversify and expand available water sources.

Complementing these efforts is the construction of water treatment facilities that will support another two deep wells, further enhancing the reliability, sustainability, and quality of water supply delivered to customers.

The utility has also intensified its aquifer and deepwell monitoring program through daily performance assessments of operating wells and monthly monitoring of Static Water Levels (SWL) and Pumping Water Levels (PWL) to support the sustainable management of groundwater resources.

To further strengthen operational reliability, Clark Water maintains an ongoing replenishment program for critical spare parts and strictly implements preventive maintenance activities across its facilities and equipment. These measures help minimize unplanned service interruptions and improve overall system performance.

Article continues after this 

Through these initiatives, Clark Water aims to help customers benefit from enhanced water security and reduced risk of service disruptions.

“Water security remains one of Clark Water’s highest priorities as we continue to support Clark’s growth as one of the country’s premier investment and economic hubs. Through proactive planning, strategic infrastructure investments, and responsible resource management, we are strengthening the resilience of our water supply system to ensure that businesses, industries, locators, and communities within Clark continue to enjoy reliable water services even during periods of extreme weather conditions such as El Niño,” says Lyn Zamora, General Manager of Clark Water.

Article continues after this 

Clark Water likewise continues to implement robust Non-Revenue Water (NRW) management programs, maintaining an average NRW level of only 6% during the first half of 2026. Key measures include proactive leak detection and rapid leak repair, optimized pressure and supply management, recalibration of tank rule curves and discharge settings, implementation of customer meter replacement programs, and the establishment of District Metered Areas (DMAs) to accurately identify, monitor, and address high-NRW zones.

Through these efforts, Clark Water continues to enhance system performance, reduce water losses, and ensure a more reliable and sustainable water supply for its customers.

Beyond infrastructure and operational initiatives, Clark Water remains committed to environmental sustainability and watershed protection.

READ: Manila Water’s robust contingency assets to boost water security

In partnership with the Clark Development Corp. (CDC), the company has actively supported watershed rehabilitation through tree-planting activities. Since 2014, Clark Water has successfully reforested a total of 10 hectares and planted 8,330 trees, contributing to biodiversity conservation and the protection of vital watershed resources that support long-term water sustainability.

World.title: Legarda calls for stronger action as child stunting rises
World.content:
Sen. Loren Legarda —Photo from her office

MANILA, Philippines — No education reform can fully succeed while Filipino children continue to suffer from chronic malnutrition during their earliest years, Sen. Loren Legarda said in a statement issued on Tuesday as she called for stronger government action to fight child stunting.

Legarda called for stronger coordination among national government agencies, local government units, schools, communities, and the private sector to fully implement nutrition and early childhood development programs, strengthen maternal healthcare, improve access to nutritious food, and ensure that every Filipino family benefits from the protections envisioned under the First 1,000 Days Law.

Citing data from the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI) of the Department of Science and Technology, Legarda said stunting among children under five rose from 23.6 percent to 25.3 percent, or about one in every four Filipino children, marking the first increase in the country’s stunting rate in a decade

Article continues after this 

The FNRI figures, highlighted by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II), show that nearly one in every four Filipino children under five is stunted, a 1.7-percentage-point jump from 2023 that reverses a downward trend that had held since 2015.

READ: Child stunting rise highlights urgency of House nutrition bill – Dy

Lasting effects of stunting

Stunting, caused by chronic undernutrition, has lasting effects on a child’s physical growth, brain development, learning capacity, and future productivity, Legarda stressed.

Data also reveal how uneven the crisis is across the country.

Stunting rates are higher in rural areas at 27.8 percent compared to 23.2 percent in urban areas, with the highest rate recorded in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao at 36 percent, followed by the Zamboanga Peninsula at 34.6 percent, the Negros Island Region at 30.9 percent, and Mimaropa at 30.3 percent.

Article continues after this 

Legarda noted that these numbers suggest that families in the most underserved and remote parts of the country carry the heaviest weight of the crisis, and that any response must reach them first.

Stunting persists among school-age kids

The senator also pointed out that the damage does not end at age five.

Article continues after this 

FNRI also found that stunting persists in 18.9 percent of school-age children between 5 and 10 years old, and in 21.4 percent of adolescents aged 10 to 19. These figures suggest that many children carry the effects of early malnutrition through their entire basic education.

“When we talk about the education crisis, we often think of classrooms, teachers, and books. But the first barrier to learning may start even before a child goes to school. If a child grows up lacking nutrition, it’s not only growth that’s affected, but also the ability to learn, to understand, to dream, and get ahead in life,” Legarda said.

The country’s efforts to address learning poverty must begin with ensuring that children receive adequate nutrition from the earliest stages of life, she stressed.

“The first 1,000 days of a child’s life, from pregnancy until the age of two, lay the foundation for lifelong learning and development. If we cannot give importance to this period, it’s harder to chase the opportunities lost. The fight against stunting is a fight for the future of every Filipino child,” Legarda said.

READ: Study: 1 in 4 Filipino kids under age 5 stunted – News

Inseparable link between nutrition and education

Legarda has long championed policies that recognize the inseparable link between nutrition, health, and education.

As author and co-sponsor of the Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act (Republic Act No. 11148), she pushed for the institutionalization of a comprehensive national strategy that would provide health and nutrition interventions during the first 1,000 days of a child’s life, widely recognized as the most critical period for physical and cognitive development.

Building on this reform, Legarda is the principal author of Senate Bill No. 792, or the proposed Breast Milk Banking Act, to establish a National Breast Milk Banking Strategy, expand regional human milk banks and satellite facilities nationwide, and ensure the safe collection, screening, processing, storage, and distribution of donated breast milk.

The measure aims to make safe donor breast milk accessible to infants who cannot receive an adequate supply from their own mothers, with priority determined according to medical and nutritional need.

She has also filed Senate Bill No. 1853 or the proposed K to 3 Foundational Learning and Nurturing Care Act, which seeks to strengthen literacy, numeracy, socio-emotional learning, and values formation from Kindergarten to Grade 3 while ensuring that health, nutrition, and responsive caregiving remain integral to every child’s learning journey.

Recognizing that stunting is also driven by unstable access to affordable, nutritious food, Legarda principally authored Senate Bill No. 2051, or the proposed Local Harvest Support Act, which can support school-based feeding and nutrition programs, including DepEd’s School-Based Feeding Program and hospital dietary services, to source food from farmers and fisherfolk within or near their communities.

The measure also establishes a National Rescue-Buy Program to stabilize farmgate prices during market disruptions, ensuring that families, particularly in rural and underserved areas where stunting rates are highest, have consistent access to fresh, affordable produce.

“In many villages, the parents of these children are farmers and fishers. If schools buy from them, we can properly feed the children and the earnings of their families so that they can have nutritious food at home. This is the cycle we want to address,” Legarda said.

Throughout her years in the Senate, Legarda has consistently advocated for greater investments in maternal and child health, school-based nutrition programs, food security, and quality education, recognizing that these are interconnected pillars of human development.

Legarda said that investing in nutrition is essential to building a healthier, more educated, and more productive nation, as chronic malnutrition continues to hamper learning outcomes, economic opportunities, and efforts to reduce poverty.

“No parent wants their children to go hungry and be left behind. Every day, millions of Filipino families are working hard to support their children and be able to serve nutritious food at their tables. We should not let them take up the fight alone. Investing in the nutrition of the youth is investing in the strength, intelligence, and the abilities of every Filipino family,” Legarda said.

World.title: Pasay police explains confrontation with photojournalists covering rally
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The Pasay City Police Station explained why some of its personnel confronted at least two photojournalists covering a rally outside an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) meeting held there on Wednesday.

“Our police officers heard something bad. So, our police officers tried to restrict whoever said it,” Pasay police chief Col. Joselito de Sesto detailed in an interview on DZMM on Wednesday night.

Although he did not specify what exactly the photojournalist had said, De Sesto claimed that cursing at the police could be considered resistance or disobedience to a person in authority.

Article continues after this 

READ: PNP probes cops over ‘harassment’ of 2 photojournalists covering rally

“Our personnel did not recognize that it was one of our friends from the media whom they had caught because he was swinging his camera, so our police held them to restrict the one who was cursing,” De Sesto said.

“When our personnel found out it was a member of the media, we let the person go,” he added.

Protesters led by the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan and other progressive groups staged a rally outside the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City during the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

As the police attempted to push back on the rallyists, photojournalists Bullit Marquez and Rene Dilan were allegedly confronted by law enforcers and prevented from photographing the arrest of protesters, according to the Photojournalists’ Center of the Philippines.

Article continues after this 

Earlier, Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. pointed the blame at the rallyists for “provoking” the police and denied harassing them during the incident, also citing that the area was a no-rally zone.

“But, we still observed maximum tolerance,” de Sesto maintained. “We didn’t fight back against the rallyists.”

Article continues after this 

In a statement, the PNP further said it will be investigating the incident and that it would be taking the “appropriate administrative and other legal actions” if it is proven that personnel failed to observe existing laws, PNP policies and operational procedures.

United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio was expected during the Asean meeting.

World.title: Government’s flagship one-stop shop launched in Maguindanao
World.content:
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. —RTVM screengrab

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday launched the Bangsamoro Convergence Program at Maguindanao del Norte. The program gathers all government services in one stop to deliver frontline government assistance across the region.

The national government turned over P3.4 billion in projects and assistance to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) during the program, which was held alongside the “Bawat Bayan Makikinabang” event.

“Complementing this initiative are the frontline services being delivered by the Bangsamoro Government. There are 15 BARMM Ministries and offices here, led by the Office of the Chief Minister that will turn over various assistance to you, at least to a thousand local beneficiaries,” said Marcos in his speech.

Article continues after this 

READ: Marcos distributes assistance in Bangsamoro region

It is aimed at improving livelihood opportunities, supporting workers and transport operators, boosting economic activity, enhancing disaster preparedness, and delivering essential services across the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region.

READ: Bangsamoro chief minister to focus on service over politics

Furthermore, the program also centered on the intergovernmental collaboration between the National and Bangsamoro Governments

Marcos also turned over checks to the provinces of BARMM under the Socio-Civic-Projects Fund to address local issues. —GENESON SATSATIN/INQUIRER.net TRAINEE

World.title: Padilla told: Prosec’s task is push case, be shocked if we defend the VP
World.content:
Senator-judge Robinhood Padilla

MANILA, Philippines — Senator-judge Robinhood Padilla has been reminded that the duty of the prosecution panel in an impeachment case revolves around pushing the case against the respondent, which in this case, is Vice President Sara Duterte.

In a press briefing on Wednesday, after the ninth day of the impeachment trial, both lead public prosecutor Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro and counsel for the prosecution Lorna Kapunan stressed that the role of the prosecution is to prosecute Duterte, and it is the defense’s duty to prove her innocence.

The two lawyers said this after Padilla, in his manifestation during the latter part of the trial, called on the prosecution to refrain from being “one-sided.” But according to Luistro, it would be a shock if the prosecution chooses neutrality—and an even bigger surprise if they defend Duterte.

Article continues after this 

“Well, with all due respect to Senator-judge Robin Padilla, apparently this impeachment trial is adversarial—it is clearly why there is a prosecution; it is (for us) to establish the case. That’s why there is a defense panel, to defend the innocence of the respondent. So it is very much anticipated that the prosecution is biased towards presenting the case, presenting the evidence,” Luistro said.

READ: Luistro tells Padilla: Conviction is not a ground to disqualify witness

“Maybe it is surprising if the prosecution will be neutral, and even more confusing if we defend the respondent,” she added.

Kapunan said that Luistro is being “very diplomatic,” suggesting that she would have given a more direct answer. Eventually, Kapunan said that it is the nature of the beast—that the prosecution prosecutes, and the defense defends.

“I think Cong. Jinky (Luistro) is very diplomatic in her answer, because if that was me, I am gentlelady but a bit rude. But I’ve always deferred; I’ve always said that sometimes the Senate impeachment hearings are in black and white, and we’re very appreciative that Senator Robin always brings color and surprise and excitement,” she said.

Article continues after this 

“But the prosecution really is for the prosecution, and the defense is for the defense. As we say, it is the nature of the beast,” she added.

Kapunan also admitted that it was them—lawyers for the prosecution—who were scolded by Padilla for disrupting his manifestation. The private lawyer reasoned that they, as members of the bar, cannot help but react to the statements issued by the Senator-judge.

Article continues after this 

READ: Lascañas’ EJK claims against Sara Duterte surface at trial

“During the hearing, we were awakened and scolded while being in the front row, so may I use this opportunity to apologize to Senator-judge Robin; there was no intent to disrespect him. But of course, if you are a lawyer and you are engaged in litigation, you sometimes show emotes, they know that,” she said.

“This is not an emote where you do drama, but it is an instinctive reaction; there was really no intent to disrespect him when he said—especially us in the front row, we stared at each other, only to find out that it was us in the front row being scolded. So Senator Robin, you said we are friends, forgive us, we won’t do it again,” she added.

Padilla made the comment that he wishes the prosecution would not be one-sided, after questioning the prosecution over the changing affidavits of former police officer Arturo Lascañas.

Lascañas’ affidavit on Duterte being one of the many architects of the past administration’s anti-drug war was brought up during discussions on the Vice President’s threat against high-ranking officials, as proof of her alleged penchant for violence.

READ: With or without contract to kill, VP made impeachable offense – lawmaker

The impeachment court has finished discussing Article IV of the Articles of Impeachment. Article IV deals with Duterte’s threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., first lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House of Representatives Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, made in an online press briefing last November 23, 2024.

In that online press briefing, Duterte was asked by a vlogger to take care, as she may be in danger. The Vice President then responded by urging people not to worry about her as she has already talked to a person about killing the Marcos couple and Romualdez if she herself gets killed.

However, several government officials and prosecutors believe it was a grave threat—regardless of whether or not the Vice President executed a contract with an assassin to kill the three. /cb

World.title: Nartatez: No ‘harassment’ as cops pushed back rallyists at Asean meeting
World.content:
Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. speaks to reporters in Pasay City on Wednesday night, July 22, 2026. (Photo by JASON SIGALES / INQUIRER.net)

MANILA, Philippines — Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. insisted that there was no harassment by law enforcers as they pushed back against a group of protesters rallying outside an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) meeting.

“The rallyists were the one provoking,” Nartatez told reporters in a chance interview in Pasay City on Wednesday night.

“Did our police officers curse at them? No such thing happened. There’s no such thing as harassment,” he said.

Article continues after this 

READ: PNP probes cops over ‘harassment’ of 2 photojournalists covering rally

“The place was a no-rally zone. We have guests, right? Asean members. Is that what you would show your guests if you had any? And they don’t have the necessary permits. We have freedom parks,” he further insisted.

Protesters led by the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan and other progressive groups staged a rally outside the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City during the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

As the police attempted to push back on the rallyists, photojournalists Bullit Marquez and Rene Dilan were reportedly confronted by law enforcers and prevented from photographing the arrest of protesters, according to the Photojournalists’ Center of the Philippines.

“There was a rally. The police engaged them. Our police officers have a calibrated response. The problem there was, of course, we won’t be able to tell who is holding the line among those who were rallying,” Nartatez explained.

Article continues after this 

One of the photojournalists’ cameras was reportedly broken during the encounter.

“There was? Then, they should go to the police station and file a complaint,” he suggested.

Article continues after this 

Earlier on Wednesday, in a statement, the PNP said it will be investigating the incident.

It vowed to take “appropriate administrative and other legal actions” if it is proven that personnel failed to observe existing laws, PNP policies and operational procedures.

United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio was expected during the Asean meeting.

World.title: Highlights:  Day 9 of Sara Duterte impeachment trial | July 22, 2026
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines – The Senate impeachment court began sending subpoenas to six banks, the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), and the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) on Wednesday for Vice President Sara Duterte’ financial records, as Day 9 proceedings wrapped up Article IV testimony and presentation of evidence.

The court ordered BIR, AMLC and six banking institutions to produce the financial records of Vice President Sara Duterte, her husband Manases Carpio, and businesses allegedly linked to them. The banks named in the subpoenas are Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co., Philippine Savings Bank, Bank of the Philippine Islands, Security Bank Corp., LandBank of the Philippines, and BDO Unibank.

READ: Highlights: Day 8 of Sara Duterte impeachment trial | July 22, 2026

Article continues after this 

The subpoenas came as the trial entered its ninth day, with the defense completing its cross-examination of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag, the prosecution’s final witness on Article IV covering Duterte’s alleged grave threats against President Marcos, first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

The prosecution concluded its nine-day presentation of Article IV, having used six of its allotted eleven days for the article itself, with the remaining days spent on other matters.

On the witness stand, Matibag told senator-judges that the search for Duterte’s alleged assassin had been narrowed to fewer than 20 individuals, adding that the bureau was finally getting close to identifying the individual or individuals involved.

The day also produced procedural friction and lighter moments.

Defense counsel Mark Vinluan and lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro clashed over whether the House committee on justice proceedings constituted a mini trial, with Luistro insisting they were only clarificatory hearings.

Article continues after this 

Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo publicly complained that senator-judges “waste time” lecturing lawyers instead of focusing on evidence.

In one of the day’s lighter moments, Matibag himself raised an objection typically made by opposing counsel during Vinluan’s questioning, prompting a reminder from the court that rulings are reserved for the senator-judges.

Article continues after this 

Outside the court

Prosecutor Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong clarified separately that identifying the alleged hitman is a matter for a separate criminal investigation and is not a condition needed to complete the evidence for Article IV in the constitutional case.

Rep. Robert Ace Barbers added that the House panel would consider all possible legal actions against Duterte after the impeachment trial, depending on what the NBI investigation yields.

A separate controversy arose over a July 7 letter from Duterte to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian requesting that the Senate shoulder catering costs sourced from the OVP’s accredited caterer during the trial.

Sen. Panfilo Lacson confirmed the OVP made the request, while defense spokesman Michael Poa said no such arrangement appeared to have been granted.

House Deputy Speaker Janette Garin called the request to have the Senate cover the costs improper, funny.

Meanwhile, Rep. Bienvenido Abante Jr. criticized Duterte for conducting a five-country personal trip while the trial is ongoing, calling the travel a “betrayal of public trust.” [10]

World.title: Almaty to Host Central Asia Fintech Summit 2026 in September
World.content:
62109

ALMATY – The Central Asia Fintech Summit (CAFS) 2026 will take place in Almaty on Sept. 11, bringing together financial institutions, fintech companies, regulators, investors and technology leaders to discuss the future of digital finance in Central Asia.

Organized by the National Payment Corporation of Kazakhstan and the National Bank of Kazakhstan, the summit will take place at Tselinny Center of Contemporary Culture from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The event is expected to serve as one of the region’s leading platforms for dialogue on financial technologies, digital assets and the development of modern financial infrastructure.

The summit will bring together representatives of the banking sector, fintech firms, international organizations, technology companies, regulators, investors and industry experts to discuss emerging trends and opportunities shaping the regional financial ecosystem.

Building on the momentum of the 2025 edition, organizers say this year’s summit aims to further strengthen cooperation across the industry. Last year’s event marked a shift from a discussion platform to a mechanism for coordinating the fintech sector, resulting in the launch of digital asset initiatives and the signing of strategic industry agreements, including those related to QR payment infrastructure.

The 2025 summit attracted more than 4,000 participants, featured over 80 speakers, and welcomed delegates from more than 30 countries.

World.title: Kazakhstan Reports Record Ice Cream Production in June
World.content:
69306

ALMATY – Kazakhstan’s ice cream production more than doubled in June compared to the same month last year, reaching nearly 20,100 tons, according to new data released by the Bureau of National Statistics. The surge comes as the country’s dairy industry continues to expand, with ice cream among the fastest-growing product categories in the first half of 2026.

The latest figures complement the bureau’s earlier report showing that Kazakhstan’s overall dairy manufacturing output increased by 11.9% in the first six months of the year, driven primarily by strong growth in cheese, butter and ice cream production.

June’s production was 116% higher than a year earlier and almost doubled compared to May. It also exceeded the previous June average of the past five years by 2.5 times and surpassed the previous monthly record of 10,800 tons, set in July 2016, by 85%.

The sharpest increase was recorded in plombir ice cream, a rich, high-butterfat vanilla ice cream, with production reaching 10,200 tons, 3.6 times higher than in June 2025 and nearly three times more than in May. Cream ice cream production also expanded, rising 75% year-on-year and 57% month-on-month to 7,500 tons.

The value of production also increased sharply. Enterprises engaged in ice cream manufacturing produced goods worth 24.3 billion tenge (US$45.4 million) in June, approximately doubling both year-on-year and month-on-month.

The sector has maintained strong momentum since late 2024. Production volumes have recorded annual growth every month since then, averaging 32% year-on-year throughout 2025 and accelerating to around 60% so far in 2026.

According to the Agriculture Ministry, Kazakhstan also became a net exporter of ice cream for the first time in its history last year, with exports exceeding imports.

World.title: Ye’s Almaty Concert Sells Half of Available Tickets During Presales
World.content:
158695

ALMATY – Around half of all tickets for American rapper Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, sold out on the first day of presales for his Aug. 14 concert in Almaty, organizers announced on July 22.

The performance at Almaty’s Central Stadium is expected to become the largest music show ever staged in Central Asia and forms part of Ye’s world tour promoting his latest album Bully.

Presales, available exclusively through the Freedom SuperApp, attracted thousands of users within minutes of opening at noon. Organizers said the lowest-priced ticket categories sold out almost immediately, with ticket prices ranging from 120,000 tenge (US$222) to 350,000 tenge (US$648). To discourage ticket scalping, purchases during presales were limited to four tickets per customer.

Virtual queue introduced to manage demand

Organizers said the online waiting room used during the launch was not a technical failure but a standard queue management system widely used by major global ticketing platforms, including Ticketmaster, AXS, See Tickets and Eventim.

The system processes customers on a first-come, first-served basis while preventing platform overload during periods of exceptionally high demand. Buyers who completed their purchase received electronic vouchers, while tickets with unique QR codes will be emailed 24 hours before the concert on Aug. 13.

In response to strong public interest, organizers also launched Fan2Fan, an official resale platform operated through Ticketon.kz. The service allows ticket holders unable to attend the concert to resell their tickets securely. Once a ticket is resold, the seller’s voucher is automatically canceled, and a new voucher is issued to the buyer, who will receive the valid QR code before the event.

Organizers warned that tickets transferred outside the official platform cannot be guaranteed, as the final QR code will be sent only to the original purchaser.

Organizers describe the concert as the largest international music event ever staged in Central Asia and expect it to attract visitors from many countries, providing a boost to event tourism and reinforcing Almaty’s position as an emerging cultural destination in the region.

First Media Group is organizing the performance as part of its efforts to bring major international music productions to Kazakhstan. According to the organizers, the show will feature a full-scale stadium production combining music, visual art, stage design and advanced technology. The setlist is expected to include songs from Ye’s latest work alongside some of his best-known hits spanning more than two decades of his career.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s Dairy Output Rises as Cheese and Ice Cream Lead Growth
World.content:
33735

ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s dairy manufacturing output rose 11.9% in the first half of 2026. The growth is concentrated in cheese, butter and ice cream while production of processed liquid milk remained nearly unchanged, according to the latest release from the Bureau of National Statistics.

The value of manufactured dairy products reached 414.9 billion tenge (US$887.4 million). Cheese and curd output reached 30,661 tons, up 26.2% year on year. Particularly noticeable growth is recorded in hard cheese output at 56.7%.

Butter and milk-spread production rose 27% to 24,376 tons, whereas ice cream output surged 64.7% to 55,199 tons in January-June. By contrast, production of processed liquid milk and cream remained almost unchanged, up just 0.4% to 331,342 tons. Yogurt and other fermented milk and cream products grew modestly at 3.2% to 134,168 tons.

Traditional fermented dairy products showed different dynamics. Kymyz (made from mare milk) production reached 774 tons, up 36.9%, while shubat (made from camel milk) production fell 42% to 509 tons.

The latest figures continue an expansion recorded in 2025, when cheese and curd production increased 18.3%, ice cream output rose 22% and processed liquid milk and cream grew 6.2%.

Last year, Kazakhstan produced dairy products worth 705.7 billion tenge (US$1.5 billion), up from 606.4 billion tenge (US$1.3 billion) a year earlier.

Dairy manufacturing remained geographically concentrated. The Almaty, North Kazakhstan and Kostanai regions together accounted for around 45.6% of Kazakhstan’s dairy manufacturing output by value in 2025.

Trade data show that rising domestic production has not eliminated Kazakhstan’s dependence on imported dairy goods. In the first five months of this year, Kazakhstan exported 859.7 tons of cheese and curd worth $3.2 million, mainly to Russia, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia. Smaller shipments also reached Azerbaijan and South Korea. Imports were far larger at 16,578.9 tons worth $81.7 million, primarily from Russia and Belarus.

Demand within Kazakhstan also increased. Domestic sales of cheese and curd reached 41,400 tons, up 11.2% from the same period a year earlier.

The figures may suggest that local producers are gaining ground around cheese production. However, imports still remain substantial, reflecting continued demand for foreign varieties and the scale advantage of producers in neighboring Russia and Belarus.

With ice cream, there is a different picture. In January-May, Kazakhstan exported $32.4 million worth of ice cream and other edible ice, exceeding imports of $19.4 million.

Kazakhstan became a net exporter of ice cream for the first time in 2025, as domestic production and exports reached record levels. The ice cream industry is highly concentrated, with Almaty Region producing roughly two-thirds of the national total. Cream-based ice cream and plombir dominate the product mix, accounting for more than 80% of output.

The government is also seeking foreign investment in higher-value dairy processing. On July 16, Agriculture Minister Aidarbek Saparov met executives from Greek company Desserta Hellas to discuss a potential project to localize cheese and dairy production in Kazakhstan, reported the ministry’s press service.

According to the ministry, Kazakhstan has 64 cheese producers and 182 dairy-processing enterprises with a combined annual capacity of around 2.7 million tons of milk. Saparov noted state support includes reimbursement of up to 25% of investment costs, interest-rate subsidies and working-capital financing at 5% annually.

World.title: Kazakhstan Steps Up Aral Restoration, Water Infrastructure and Conservation Reforms
World.content:
43234

ASTANA – Kazakhstan is accelerating restoration of the North Aral Sea while advancing large-scale water management reforms, including new reservoirs, irrigation modernization, water-saving technologies and industrial water reuse.

North Aral restoration

During a working visit to the Kyzylorda Region, Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation Nurzhan Nurzhigitov met with fishermen in the Aral district to discuss measures to preserve the North Aral Sea. He said the government, together with the World Bank, has prepared the second phase of the North Aral restoration project, which includes reconstructing the Kokaral Dam to raise the sea level and increase water storage, reported the ministry’s press service on July 17.

Since Oct. 1, 2025, Kazakhstan has directed 1.4 billion cubic meters of water into the North Aral Sea through the Syr Darya River. During the current irrigation season, water is being released into the sea at a rate of 40 cubic meters per second.

The sea’s volume has reached 23.5 billion cubic meters, while salinity has declined by 10% compared to last year to 7.9 per mille. Fishermen harvested 4,200 tons of fish during the first half of the year.

Local fishermen called for stricter enforcement of agricultural water-use limits and proposed constructing the Amanotkel hydraulic structure to increase water releases into the Syr Darya River. Nurzhigitov instructed the Water Management Committee to prepare project documentation.

Balkhash preservation

Nurzhigitov said Kazakhstan is continuing efforts to preserve Lake Balkhash. Over the past two years, around 30 billion cubic meters of water have been directed to the lake, helping stabilize its water level. A master plan for preserving the Balkhash ecosystem through 2040 is being developed with support from the French Development Agency (AFD).

Water sector modernization

The government’s water management strategy through 2030 includes construction of 42 new reservoirs, reconstruction of 37 existing reservoirs, modernization of 14,500 kilometers of irrigation canals, wider adoption of water-saving technologies, digitalization of water management, and improved flood and drought forecasting, reported Kazinform on July 20.

Agriculture accounts for around 60% of Kazakhstan’s total water withdrawals, making irrigation efficiency a key priority. By the end of 2025, water-saving technologies covered 543,500 hectares, conserving approximately 874 million cubic meters of irrigation water. The government aims to expand their use to 1.3 million hectares by 2030, saving around 2.2 billion cubic meters of water annually.

Industry, which accounts for 30% of national water consumption, is also undergoing reform. Under the new Water Code, enterprises will gradually transition to recycled and reused water systems over the next seven years, with the goal of increasing the share of reused water to 28% by 2030.

Developing human capital

The ministry has expanded water conservation education programs, reaching more than 3.3 million students this year. It has also launched nationwide campaigns to restore springs and water bodies and is carrying out digital registration of 2,772 natural springs.

Kazakhstan has expanded training for water specialists by increasing the number of universities and colleges offering water-related programs, while government-funded scholarships have risen to 1,000. Salaries at the state-owned Kazvodkhoz enterprise have more than doubled since 2024, reaching an average of 326,000 tenge.

World.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Astana Bus Brand, Begin Electric Bus Production in 2027
World.content:
36786

ASTANA – Kazakhstan will begin serial production of domestically branded buses under the Astana name in November, marking a major step in expanding the country’s automotive manufacturing, Astana Motors Chairman Nurlan Smagulov announced at a government meeting on July 21.

The project is one of the company’s flagship initiatives aimed at broadening Kazakhstan’s lineup of locally produced vehicles. The buses were developed with Chinese technology partners and incorporate components from leading global manufacturers, while Kazakh engineers contributed to their design. Production will take place in Kazakhstan.

Serial production of diesel and compressed natural gas (CNG) buses is scheduled to start in November, according to the Prime Minister’s press service.

Smagulov also announced that the company is developing a line of electric vehicles with Chinese automaker BYD using new-generation battery technology. Production of Astana-branded electric buses is expected to begin in March 2027.

World.title: Shanghai and Technology Turn in Kazakhstan-China Relations
World.content:
20188

Kazakhstan’s largest Chinese business round in years put data, computing and digital logistics at the center. The measure of it will be deployment.

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s working visit to Shanghai on July 16-17 produced a familiar number and a new emphasis. Kazakhstan and China signed more than 70 commercial documents worth over $15 billion, covering artificial intelligence, transport, finance, agriculture and machinery. What set this round apart was where the weight fell. The center of gravity sat in data, computing and digital logistics, the fields that will define the next decade of the relationship, rather than in the oil, metals and transit flows that built it.

Tokayev opened the roundtable with the figures that anchor the partnership and a phrase to frame them. The two countries, he said, have entered a new “golden thirty years.” Bilateral trade reached $49 billion in 2025, a record, and Chinese firms have put more than $30 billion into the Kazakh economy, with over 8,500 enterprises carrying Chinese capital now active in the country. He named CNPC, CITIC and Huawei among the anchors, then pointed to a newer industrial layer: a gas chemical complex with Sinopec, a corn processing plant with Fufeng and a textile cluster with Lihua, alongside multi-brand vehicle assembly for Changan, Great Wall Motor and Chery. The value of Chinese participation, in his telling, sits increasingly in jobs, technology and industrial depth, with raw trade volume the older part of the story.

The pivot to data and computing

The signing list showed the shift in plain terms. Huawei took the largest share, concluding a strategic partnership with the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development and a separate equipment supply agreement with Samruk-Kazyna. Kazakhtelecom signed a framework with Hengtong Group on Data Center Valley, the gigawatt-scale computing complex rising near Ekibastuz. Almaty gained an artificial intelligence and robotics agreement involving UBTECH, and Kazakh universities tied up with Shanghai and Suzhou institutions. The timing was deliberate. The visit opened alongside the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, where Astana joined 29 governments in the Shanghai-based World AI Cooperation Organization.

Data Center Valley is where Kazakhstan’s positioning becomes legible. The same Ekibastuz site that now draws Chinese fibre and construction capital also anchors a $10 billion arrangement with Nvidia and a US-linked cloud partner, reported earlier this summer. Astana is not committing to one technology ecosystem. It is inviting both and pricing the same underlying assets into each: land, spare grid capacity and electricity near $0.025 per kilowatt-hour. Power that is scarce and expensive in the United States and Europe is abundant and cheap in northern Kazakhstan, and the government is monetizing that gap across the very rivalry that constrains hyperscale expansion elsewhere.

Mobility and ports rounded out the industrial side. Allur signed to build Li Auto vehicles in Kazakhstan, Astana Motors licensed Omoda and Jaecoo assembly with Chery, and Samruk-Kazyna, Freedom Holding and Astana’s city administration agreed a framework with Geely on electric-vehicle charging and automotive AI. On the Caspian, Guoyou committed to a multifunctional terminal at Kuryk, the port that feeds Kazakh cargo onto the Trans-Caspian route. In parallel talks, Tokayev discussed a first Central Asian battery plant with CATL. Each of these keeps more of the manufacturing chain inside the country.

Corridors, minerals and the deployment question

The logistics agenda followed the same logic. About 85% of China-Europe rail traffic already crosses Kazakhstan, and freight with China rose roughly 9% in the first half of 2026 to 18.7 million tons, while container trains dispatched from China through the country climbed more than a third year on year. In Shanghai, Tokayev sold the next layer, a digital one: Smart Cargo, a single window pooling customs, logistics and commercial data, built so that goods clear borders at something closer to the speed at which data moves. The framing matters because the Middle Corridor’s physical ceiling is fixed. Two changes of rail gauge and a Caspian crossing keep it structurally more expensive than the all-water route to Europe. Additional value has to come from speed, transparency and digital integration, since the geography will not yield maritime-scale tonnage.

Critical minerals formed the other pillar. Tokayev restated the demand Kazakhstan now makes of every partner it courts, which is processing and manufacturing capacity on Kazakh soil, with extraction rights as the opening term rather than the prize. That message runs alongside Astana’s parallel engagement with Washington and Brussels on rare earth separation and refining. It is also the message the Shanghai deals encode. The stated goal across them is technology transfer, research centres and production chains, with capital treated as the entry ticket.

The authors are Alexander Dergay, a column writer for Berliner Zeitung and the Ostdeutsche Allgemeine, and Eldaniz Gusseinov, a co-founder and head of research at Nightingale Int.
